openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-21-add-iphone-ble-client/specs/iphone-ble-teleoperation/spec.md

iphone ble teleoperation

iPhone BLE teleoperation delta

Purpose

Lets an iPhone user control the normal product car over its existing BLE API with explicit arming, bounded touch intent and visible limits on connection and physical-state evidence.

ADDED Requirements

Supported web delivery

The controller SHALL run as an HTTPS page with Bluefy as its supported iPhone BLE host. It SHALL check the picker API before selection and required GATT read/notify and explicit write modes before writes; missing support SHALL disable control with an explanation. V1 SHALL use buttons without requesting motion-sensor permission. Published assets SHALL contain no secrets or third-party runtime scripts.

Unsupported host
  • WHEN the page opens without required Web Bluetooth APIs, including in an unsupported Safari session, or without HTTPS
  • THEN it explains that supported Bluefy/HTTPS is required and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoints

Explicit discovery and selection

The client SHALL invoke the browser device picker only from an explicit Choose & Connect action while active. It SHALL select the existing name-only advertisement without requiring an advertised service UUID, request access to the product service, and connect only to the chosen device. The picker SHALL NOT be described as a claim; GATT connection is the claim. Cancellation/no result SHALL NOT be described as proof that the car is busy.

Browser selection precedes connection
  • WHEN Choose & Connect opens the browser picker, including when same-name candidates exist
  • THEN no GATT connection occurs until the user selects a candidate, and the page does not auto-select a remembered device
  • AND the action explains that connecting claims the car and switches off its Wi-Fi AP; the page does not promise picker RSSI or distinguishable hardware addresses
Picker cancelled or completed after local cancellation
  • WHEN the picker is cancelled, has no selection, or returns after the local attempt was cancelled
  • THEN no connection is started; a new manual action is required
  • AND the page does not claim it can impose a scan timeout or forcibly dismiss the browser picker

Validate the connected car

Setup SHALL start locally disarmed at zero. Before regular streaming, the client SHALL validate GATT properties, 27-byte version-1 capabilities, positive finite geometry, finite nonnegative limits, nonzero windows, lease >=500 ms, claim >=1000 ms, valid Claimed/Stopped Status and an initial 72-byte zero write submission. Setup SHALL finish within 10 seconds of GATT connect invocation or end through cleanup. It SHALL send no ARM or nonzero setpoint.

Unsupported payload or capabilities
  • WHEN required characteristics/properties or capabilities are invalid, windows are unsupported, or the initial 72-byte submission is rejected
  • THEN the client reports incompatibility and attempts disconnect without fragmentation, protocol substitution or automatic reconnect
  • AND a resolved without-response write is not displayed as proof of device receipt or measured MTU
Claim expires during setup
  • WHEN discovery/subscription takes longer than the car's claim window and the car releases the connection
  • THEN setup fails without automatic reconnect, even if the local 10-second deadline has not passed

Existing BLE wire contract

The client SHALL use the existing product UUIDs and write each setpoint as one 72-byte value: little-endian u32 sequence plus 68-byte little-endian TwistStamped CDR, empty frame, zero timestamp, and only vx/vy/wz nonzero. Sequences SHALL advance with wrapping u32 ordering per connection. ARM/STOP SHALL use one-byte values 1/2 with response. BLE SHALL have no UDP header, numeric session ID, HELLO or BYE.

Wire values agree with the product
  • WHEN zero, each direction and a sequence wrapping from 4294967295 to 0 are encoded
  • THEN bytes match the existing Rust/Python product vectors and the unused Twist fields are zero
  • AND a new connection starts a new sequence history

Explicit zero then ARM

Only a new user ARM action SHALL initiate arming. It SHALL invalidate all touches, stream fresh zero and send ARM once. Local motion permission SHALL require both successful completion of that ARM write and a subsequent fresh Status read reporting Armed/none/none within one second of the action. A notification alone SHALL NOT grant motion. Failure, refusal or timeout SHALL clear intent and end through cleanup; late callbacks SHALL NOT arm locally.

Touch predates ARM
  • GIVEN a direction is held while locally disarmed
  • WHEN ARM succeeds
  • THEN only zero is sent until that touch is released and a new direction press begins
ARM is refused or its confirmation is late
  • WHEN ARM returns an ATT error or its write/Status confirmation misses the one-second deadline
  • THEN the client remains locally disarmed and requires a new connection and explicit ARM before motion

Gentle single-axis directions

V1 input SHALL use six hold buttons: forward/back, left/right strafe and counter-clockwise/clockwise rotation in base_link. Each press SHALL select one axis only: translation magnitude min(0.1 m/s, advertised axis maximum), rotation min(0.3 rad/s, advertised maximum). Zero-limit axes SHALL be disabled. Multiple simultaneous direction touches SHALL request zero and require all direction touches released before a new press; velocities SHALL NOT combine.

Direction mapping respects limits
  • WHEN each direction is held after successful ARM
  • THEN forward/back use +/-vx, left/right +/-vy, counter-clockwise/clockwise +/-wz, with other fields zero and advertised limits respected
  • AND max_vx=0.05 yields forward vx=0.05, while max_vy=0 disables both strafe controls

Hold cancellation and input expiry

Nonzero intent SHALL require a tracked press inside one direction control while active and locally armed. Release, leaving its bounds, cancellation or lost tracking SHALL clear intent before the next send. Hold renewal SHALL expire after 250 ms on a monotonic clock; the transmitter SHALL NOT renew input itself. Release/expiry SHALL send zero and require a new press, retaining local arm; STOP/interruption SHALL require re-arm and a new press.

Finger release or missing renewals
  • WHEN a held direction ends, is cancelled, slides outside, or has no renewal for 250 ms
  • THEN the next setpoint is zero and no buffered motion is played back
  • AND sliding back inside does not resume motion without a new press

Periodic latest-intent stream

After setup the client SHALL attempt one latest setpoint every 50 ms, zero when locally disarmed, awaiting ARM or without valid hold intent. It SHALL check lifecycle, stops and expiry before sending, allow at most one pending setpoint write promise and retain no motion backlog. A scheduler gap or interval without submitting a setpoint of >=200 ms SHALL revoke local arm and end through cleanup, without catch-up motion. Write rejection SHALL end the session.

Transport backpressure
  • GIVEN a nonzero hold and a pending write prevents another submission
  • WHEN that procedure completes before the 200 ms failure bound
  • THEN the next send uses only current unexpired intent, with no accumulated writes
  • AND completion at or after the bound cannot resume motion; a promise resolving does not confirm applied wheel motion

Validate Status and link health

The client SHALL validate three-byte Status codes and state/reason consistency, subscribe to changes and schedule a Status read every 500 ms while ready, with at most one transaction pending. A transaction taking >=1000 ms, malformed Status, GATT error, Open Status or unexpected Armed Status SHALL revoke local motion and end through cleanup. Stopped Status SHALL revoke local arm. Callbacks from old connections or cancelled operations SHALL NOT change the current session.

Silence and old callbacks
  • WHEN Status is unchanged without notifications
  • THEN reads refresh its observation age; missing a read deadline ends the session
  • AND an Armed callback from an earlier connection cannot authorize a newly connected session

STOP and re-arm latch

STOP SHALL remain available throughout a connected session, clear intent immediately and request Control=2 with response. It SHALL override ARM and touch input. Confirmation SHALL require successful STOP write completion and a subsequent fresh Stopped/Stop/none Status read within one second. Confirmed STOP or reported safety stop SHALL require explicit ARM and a new press before motion; unconfirmed STOP SHALL end through cleanup. Zero alone SHALL NOT be described as STOP.

STOP races with ARM and touch
  • WHEN STOP occurs while ARM is pending or direction events are queued
  • THEN pending local arming is invalidated, queued direction input is discarded, and any late Armed result cannot enable motion
  • AND after confirmed STOP the client may keep streaming zero to retain ownership until manual re-arm or Disconnect

Active foreground and manual recovery

During a connected session, blur/hidden/pagehide, host inactivity, observed permission/service loss or Bluetooth failure SHALL clear holds, revoke local arm and end through cleanup. Return/reload/restoration SHALL require manual Choose & Connect and ARM, never automatic recovery/replay. A pending picker SHALL NOT connect while inactive. If inactive UI stops renewing input, expiry SHALL clear motion even while transmission runs. Sustained inactive motion SHALL fail host acceptance.

Lock or Bluetooth loss while holding
  • WHEN the phone locks, changes app, or loses Bluetooth while a direction is held
  • THEN observed inactivity/loss clears motion before another send, and foreground return cannot resume the hold
  • AND if execution or UI renewal stops without an event, input expiry or the independent firmware lease stops motion; runnable cleanup is not promised after suspension/termination
  • AND phone checks must reject a host that keeps renewing nonzero motion while inactive

Bounded best-effort shutdown

Disconnect, setup failure, interruption and handled failure SHALL clear intent and stop normal writes, then independently attempt zero and STOP where supported, and local cancellation, within 500 ms total while runnable. Cancellation SHALL still be attempted if a write fails or never completes. The UI SHALL distinguish attempted, device-reported STOP and local disconnect; it SHALL NOT infer physical wheel stop or immediate ownership release from a write or cancellation.

Shutdown cannot complete its writes
  • WHEN zero is blocked or STOP receives no completion
  • THEN local cancellation is requested by the shared 500 ms deadline without waiting indefinitely
  • AND late callbacks are ignored and stop/release remain unconfirmed

Visible state and evidence limits

The UI SHALL show selected device name/available opaque ID, connection phase, local arm, limits, 72-byte packet size, requested vx/vy/wz and last-reported state/reason/error with age. Unexposed MTU/capacity SHALL be labelled unavailable. Controls SHALL have text/accessibility labels, adequate targets and cues beyond color; accessibility activation SHALL NOT latch motion. Docs SHALL identify approximate open-loop references and separate Linux fake/browser evidence from phone/radio/wheel evidence.

Reported Armed does not mean moving wheels
  • WHEN last-reported Status is Armed but no direction is held, or interruption revoked local permission
  • THEN requested motion is zero, Status retains its observation age, and the UI does not claim measured speed, live wheel state or certified emergency stopping

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-22-add-iphone-physical-control/specs/iphone-ble-teleoperation/spec.md

iphone ble teleoperation

RENAMED Requirements

  • FROM: ### Requirement: Gentle single-axis directions
  • TO: ### Requirement: Gentle input modes

MODIFIED Requirements

Supported web delivery

The controller SHALL run as an HTTPS page with Bluefy as its supported iPhone BLE host. It SHALL check the picker API before selection and required GATT read/notify and explicit write modes before writes; missing support SHALL disable control with an explanation. Buttons SHALL be the default; only a user selection of Physical mode or explicit sensor retry may request sensor permission. Published assets SHALL contain no secrets or third-party runtime scripts.

Unsupported host
  • WHEN the page opens without required Web Bluetooth APIs, including in an unsupported Safari session, or without HTTPS
  • THEN it explains that supported Bluefy/HTTPS is required and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoints

Gentle input modes

Buttons SHALL retain six single-axis hold directions; multiple touches yield zero until all release and a new press. Physical mode SHALL combine calibrated forward/back tilt as vx, side tilt as vy and heading offset as wz. Each axis SHALL remain within min(0.1 m/s, advertised translation maximum) or min(0.3 rad/s, advertised rotation maximum). Zero-limit axes SHALL stay zero; button velocities SHALL NOT combine.

Direction mapping respects limits
  • WHEN each direction is held after successful ARM
  • THEN forward/back use +/-vx, left/right +/-vy, counter-clockwise/clockwise +/-wz, with other fields zero and advertised limits respected
  • AND max_vx=0.05 yields forward vx=0.05, while max_vy=0 disables both strafe controls
Physical movement combines without exceeding per-axis limits
  • WHEN explicitly started Physical control supplies forward, left and counter-clockwise offsets after successful ARM
  • THEN vx, vy and wz may be positive together, each within its gentle and advertised maximum
  • AND a zero advertised axis stays zero without disabling other permitted components

Explicit zero then ARM

ARM SHALL require a new user action; Physical ARM SHALL capture neutral from fresh valid sensors in that action. It SHALL invalidate touches, stream fresh zero and send ARM once. Local motion permission SHALL require the ARM write and a subsequent fresh Status read reporting Armed/none/none within one second. A notification alone SHALL NOT grant motion. Failure, refusal or timeout SHALL clear intent and end through cleanup; late callbacks SHALL NOT arm locally.

Touch predates ARM
  • GIVEN a direction is held while locally disarmed
  • WHEN ARM succeeds
  • THEN only zero is sent until that touch is released and a new direction press begins
ARM is refused or its confirmation is late
  • WHEN ARM returns an ATT error or its write/Status confirmation misses the one-second deadline
  • THEN the client remains locally disarmed and requires a new connection and explicit ARM before motion
One explicit Physical action captures neutral and arms
  • WHEN sensors are enabled while disarmed
  • THEN no ARM or nonzero setpoint is sent
  • AND a subsequent explicit Set neutral & ARM captures the current fresh screen-up pose without a separate calibration tap, sends zero then ARM and requires a separate post-arm START action
  • AND missing/stale/invalid sensors or an invalid neutral posture refuse ARM locally without an ARM write

Hold cancellation and input expiry

Buttons nonzero intent SHALL require one tracked press inside a direction control while active and locally armed. Release, bounds exit, cancellation, lost tracking or multiple touches SHALL clear intent before the next send. Only UI renewal may extend the 250 ms monotonic hold deadline. Buttons retain arm after expiry and require a new press. Physical control SHALL use the explicit START/PAUSE gate and independent foreground renewal deadline instead of a held pointer.

Finger release or missing renewals
  • WHEN a held direction ends, is cancelled, slides outside, or has no renewal for 250 ms
  • THEN the next setpoint is zero and no buffered motion is played back
  • AND sliding back inside does not resume motion without a new press

Periodic latest-intent stream

After setup the client SHALL attempt one latest setpoint every 50 ms, zero when locally disarmed, awaiting ARM, without a valid Buttons hold or while Physical control is paused. It SHALL check lifecycle/stops/expiry before sending, allow one pending setpoint write and retain no motion backlog. A scheduler gap or interval without submission of >=200 ms SHALL revoke local arm and end through cleanup, without catch-up motion. Write rejection SHALL end the session.

Transport backpressure
  • GIVEN nonzero intent and a pending write prevents another submission
  • WHEN that procedure completes before the 200 ms failure bound
  • THEN the next send uses only current unexpired intent, with no accumulated writes
  • AND completion at or after the bound cannot resume motion; a promise resolving does not confirm applied wheel motion

Visible state and evidence limits

The UI SHALL show selected device name/available ID, phase, local arm, limits, packet size, requested vx/vy/wz and reported state/reason/error with age. Unexposed MTU/capacity SHALL be labelled unavailable. Controls SHALL have text/accessibility labels, adequate targets and cues beyond color. Buttons accessibility activation SHALL NOT latch motion; explicit Physical START/PAUSE activation SHALL match a tap. Docs SHALL separate approximate references, host tests, phone/radio and wheel evidence.

Reported Armed does not mean moving wheels
  • WHEN reported Status is Armed but no button direction is held and Physical control is paused, or interruption revoked local permission
  • THEN requested motion is zero, Status retains its observation age, and the UI does not claim measured speed, live wheel state or certified emergency stopping

ADDED Requirements

Visible control status

Local arm state, STOP, Physical START/PAUSE, requested motion and the latest session message SHALL remain visible while scrolling, including after fault disconnect. Physical mode SHALL show running/paused state and explain unavailable input. Scroll SHALL clear button holds and pause Physical control before another send, preserving arm/neutral. Real lifecycle and stream failures SHALL retain cleanup. Posture faults SHALL identify the angle, observed value and limit.

Scroll while armed at zero
  • WHEN the user scrolls while Physical control is paused
  • THEN arm state, STOP and the session reason stay visible, intent remains zero and scrolling alone does not disconnect
  • AND a genuine stream or lifecycle failure still disarms and displays its reason

Explicit physical sensor setup

Physical sensor setup SHALL begin only from an active user selection of Physical mode or explicit Retry action, with feature detection and permission handling. Missing/denied/failed permission or missing finite alpha/beta/gamma SHALL prevent physical motion. Late permission results or callbacks from an earlier mode, enable attempt or closed session SHALL NOT change current input. Sensor events SHALL NOT select a device, ARM or write BLE.

Denial and delayed permission response
  • WHEN permission is denied or resolves after switching to Buttons or leaving the page
  • THEN no Physical running state or calibration becomes valid and no automatic connection or ARM occurs
  • AND Buttons remain available without sensor permission

Physical calibration and angle mapping

Each explicit Physical ARM SHALL calibrate fresh finite orientation while locally disarmed with no pending control. Neutral beta/gamma SHALL be within ±30° with screen up. Shortest offsets SHALL map negative beta to forward, negative gamma to left strafe, positive alpha to left rotation, with 3° dead zones and linear scale to saturation at 20°. Held heading offset SHALL sustain rotation; neutral SHALL request zero. No silent recentering is allowed.

Heading wrap and sustained twist
  • WHEN calibrated alpha is 350° and current alpha is 10° while Physical control is explicitly running
  • THEN the heading offset is +20°, requesting capped positive wz rather than a −340° turn
  • AND fresh unchanged samples sustain that request, returning to neutral zeros it, and gyro rotation rate is not integrated
Neutral posture and operating envelope
  • WHEN calibration beta or gamma exceeds ±30°, or running Physical control has current beta/gamma beyond ±60° or heading offset beyond ±90°, or the screen orientation changes
  • THEN calibration or motion is rejected with an explanation
  • AND an armed or arming Physical session loses calibration and ends through cleanup, with manual recovery required
Reading posture while paused
  • WHEN Physical control is paused and the phone leaves the operating envelope
  • THEN intent remains zero and START is unavailable, preserving arm and neutral
  • AND returning to valid fresh input permits only a new explicit START at neutral; it neither recenters nor resumes driving

Independent physical sample freshness

Only new valid orientation events SHALL renew a 250 ms monotonic sample deadline. Expiry during running Physical control SHALL be checked before replacing a sample and end through cleanup before another nonzero send. Paused gaps SHALL preserve arm/neutral at zero and reject START until fresh input returns. Invalid input or changed reference SHALL revoke calibration and end armed/arming sessions. UI frames, stream ticks and cached values SHALL NOT renew samples or restart driving.

Sensor stops while UI and stream continue
  • WHEN no valid orientation arrives for 250 ms while Physical control and the transmitter continue running
  • THEN requested motion becomes zero, calibration and local arm are revoked, and cleanup begins
  • AND a late sample or resumed UI cannot restore motion without manual recovery
Sensor pause while paused
  • WHEN orientation pauses with Physical control paused, but the foreground and BLE stream remain healthy
  • THEN no motion is permitted until new valid input returns, while arm and neutral remain
  • AND an attempted START during the pause cannot start motion when readings return; a new explicit START at neutral is required

Explicit control mode switching

The same client SHALL expose Buttons and Physical modes, default Buttons without persistence. Every actual mode change SHALL clear both inputs and calibration, disable sensor collection and revoke local arm. A ready session SHALL supersede pending ARM with STOP; setup/picker attempts SHALL be cancelled. New mode selection SHALL NOT ARM or restore a hold; fresh prerequisites, ARM and post-arm input action are required.

Switch while Physical is running or ARM is pending
  • WHEN the user changes modes while Physical control is running or awaiting ARM completion
  • THEN no later old running state, sample or ARM result can authorize motion in the new mode
  • AND a ready connection may remain at zero after confirmed STOP until a fresh explicit ARM

Tap-based Physical driving

Physical control SHALL stay paused after ARM. START SHALL require active foreground, confirmed arm, fresh calibration and three offsets within ±3°. Running needs no held touch. PAUSE/scroll SHALL clear intent before the next send, retaining arm/neutral. ARM, STOP, mode changes and cleanup SHALL clear running state. Only UI frames may renew its 250 ms deadline; expiry SHALL revoke calibration and end through cleanup. Only a new explicit START may restart it.

Start, tilt and pause without holding
  • WHEN the user taps START at neutral after ARM, releases the screen and tilts the phone
  • THEN fresh input supplies bounded motion without a held pointer and the persistent control reads PAUSE
  • AND PAUSE yields zero while retaining local arm and neutral; returning sensor data or neutral alone does not restart driving
Neutral and explicit restart are required
  • WHEN START occurs before ARM confirmation, while sensors are stale, or outside ±3° of calibrated neutral
  • THEN no running state or nonzero intent is granted, and later data/ARM completion cannot replay that START
  • AND after pause/scroll or a new ARM, motion requires a new explicit START at neutral
Foreground renewal stops independently of sensors
  • WHEN Physical control is running and no UI frame renews its deadline for 250 ms while fresh sensors and the stream continue
  • THEN intent becomes zero and local arm/calibration are revoked through cleanup
  • AND resumed frames and samples cannot restart driving or reconnect

Mobile controller layout

The controller SHALL present labelled Buttons/Physical segmented radios, requested motion and connection/arm/driving states. At 320×568 through 390×844 CSS pixels, six Buttons directions and requested motion SHALL fit above a persistent thumb-reachable ARM/START/PAUSE and STOP dock. Sensor setup SHALL be implicit in choosing Physical; Retry appears only when needed. Protocol/raw sensor details SHALL be collapsed by default; opening diagnostics SHALL clear input without ARM or restart.

Drive without scrolling through setup details
  • WHEN the connected controller is viewed in either mode on the supported portrait sizes
  • THEN the current primary action and STOP remain visible, and requested motion is readable without opening diagnostics
  • AND Buttons keeps held directions while Physical keeps explicit neutral-gated START/PAUSE; choosing modes still disarms
Larger text and keyboard access
  • WHEN text is enlarged to 200%, a keyboard selects modes, or a narrow/landscape viewport is used
  • THEN controls remain labelled, targets at least 44×44 CSS pixels, content can scroll without horizontal overflow and focus is not covered by the dock
  • AND light/dark themes have readable text, motion is reduced when requested and no sensor or Bluetooth permission is requested by initial page load
Diagnostics while Physical is running
  • WHEN connection diagnostics are opened during Physical driving
  • THEN input becomes zero and stays paused without losing neutral/arm or disconnecting solely because details opened
  • AND closing details or returning readings cannot resume driving; a new explicit START at neutral is needed

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-22-add-laptop-ble-teleoperation/specs/laptop-teleoperation/spec.md

laptop teleoperation

MODIFIED Requirements

Explicit connection without motion

The client SHALL require an interactive terminal and exactly one transport: explicit UDP IPv4:port or BLE discovery with optional MAC. Each UDP attempt SHALL validate HELLO's nonzero session/capabilities and use fresh control sequences. BLE SHALL validate GATT/capabilities before controls. All connections SHALL start disarmed at zero. BUSY/unavailable targets SHALL retry without motion; invalid capabilities or leases below 200 ms SHALL fail.

Connection starts disarmed
  • WHEN an operator connects to a valid UDP or BLE target
  • THEN the client displays negotiated limits and connection identity and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Refused or unsupported connection
  • WHEN UDP returns BUSY, its one-second handshake expires, or BLE discovery/connect fails
  • THEN the client retries with no ARM or nonzero setpoint
  • AND invalid capabilities or an unsupported lease terminate through cleanup
Old handshake cannot reconnect
  • WHEN a UDP ACK from an earlier attempt arrives during a new handshake
  • THEN it cannot establish the new session

Bounded shutdown and honest reporting

Space SHALL clear motion and request STOP; quit, Ctrl-C, EOF and fatal errors SHALL exit through cleanup. Recoverable link errors SHALL clean up before retrying. UDP cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP and BYE within 500 ms total even if an earlier send fails. Exit SHALL restore terminal settings. Matching stopped/Stop Status SHALL be required for STOP acknowledgement. Unacknowledged STOP and BYE SHALL be labelled attempts, never verified wheel stop or release.

Cleanup tolerates a failed send
  • WHEN sending zero or STOP fails during UDP cleanup
  • THEN BYE and terminal restoration are still attempted within the cleanup deadline

Validate and correlate device input

The client SHALL validate device payload lengths and codes. UDP replies SHALL match the selected endpoint, version and current session, with Status matching a pending control sequence or unsolicited zero. BLE input SHALL belong to the current connection generation and its native GATT operation. Wrong-peer, malformed, stale or unmatched input SHALL not authorize motion or extend deadlines. Unsolicited stopped Status SHALL disable local motion before the next send.

Queued notification precedes an ARM reply
  • WHEN a stopped notification arrives before the matching ARM reply/readback
  • THEN the client clears motion and does not confuse the notification with successful ARM
Intruder packet cannot enable movement
  • WHEN another endpoint, session or closed BLE connection sends Armed Status
  • THEN local arming remains unchanged

Observable commands and evidence limits

The client SHALL show connection/local-arm state, UDP session or BLE connection generation, last valid device Status/reply age and requested vx/vy/wz. Last-reported Status SHALL be distinguished from live physical state; Echo SHALL not refresh Status age. Documentation SHALL identify open-loop speeds as approximate and cleanup as best effort. Simulator/fake-GATT passes SHALL not count as wheel, radio or electrical acceptance.

A responsive rebooted device does not prove ownership
  • GIVEN a UDP car reboots and answers Echo but does not accept the old session
  • WHEN the client displays its state
  • THEN it shows Status as last reported with its original age, sends no new HELLO merely because Echo replies, and does not claim ownership recovery

ADDED Requirements

BLE target and GATT validation

BLE SHALL discover/connect within five seconds each, select one advertising Rovi M8 or an explicit MAC, and pin that address for retries. Ambiguous names SHALL fail. Before controls it SHALL validate the car service, characteristic properties, capabilities and 72-byte write-without-response capacity (ATT MTU at least 75). Incompatible GATT SHALL fail closed.

Unsafe or ambiguous peer cannot move
  • WHEN discovery is ambiguous, the service is missing, or setpoint capacity is below 72 bytes
  • THEN the client reports the limitation, disconnects any connection and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Name discovery pins the device for recovery
  • GIVEN name discovery selected one device
  • WHEN its connection drops and another Rovi M8 advertises
  • THEN retries target the original device's MAC and cannot roam to the other car

BLE control confirmation and callback lifetime

BLE SHALL use native u32-sequenced setpoints and ARM/STOP bytes. ARM SHALL send zero first, succeed at ATT level and obtain fresh Armed/clear Status before enabling local motion. Notifications alone SHALL not authorize ARM. STOP, a safety notification or newer intent SHALL invalidate a pending ARM confirmation. Callbacks/Echo from an earlier connection generation SHALL not affect current state. Malformed Status SHALL not authorize motion.

Stop wins over an in-flight ARM
  • WHEN Space or a safety stop arrives while an ARM write/readback is pending
  • THEN the eventual Armed readback cannot re-enable local motion
Closed connection callback arrives late
  • WHEN an old connection's Armed Status or Echo notification arrives after reconnect
  • THEN it cannot arm, satisfy current Echo or change current Status

BLE loss and recovery

BLE SHALL check matched Echo every 250 ms with a 500 ms deadline. Disconnect, GATT timeout or missing Echo SHALL clear intent, attempt bounded cleanup, alert once per outage and retry after one second. Initial and recovered connections SHALL require a fresh matching Echo before accepting R. Recovery SHALL discard outage input, start disarmed and require a new R and subsequent direction. Quit SHALL work during discovery, setup and retry.

Link returns with old keys pending
  • WHEN BLE reconnects after R/motion were typed during loss
  • THEN it reports reconnected disarmed only after matching Echo
  • AND it stays zero until fresh R and direction; failed retries do not repeat the loss beep

BLE ownership and shutdown

BLE connection SHALL be treated as the ownership claim and its lifetime as identity, without invented UDP session/release acknowledgements. Only the latest intent and a single pending control action SHALL be retained. Cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP/readback and disconnect within 500 ms total, even when earlier operations fail. Successful disconnect SHALL be reported separately from physical stop. The client SHALL not manage Wi-Fi policy or switch transports automatically.

Write fails during cleanup
  • WHEN zero or STOP fails or times out
  • THEN disconnect and terminal restoration are still attempted within their bounds
  • AND missing confirmation is reported honestly

laptop teleoperation

RENAMED Requirements

  • FROM: ### Requirement: Link checks without automatic recovery
  • TO: ### Requirement: Link checks with disarmed recovery

MODIFIED Requirements

Explicit connection without motion

The client SHALL require an explicit IPv4 target/port and an interactive terminal. Each attempt SHALL claim with version-1 UDP HELLO and validate the nonzero session and capabilities. It SHALL start disarmed at zero. BUSY and a one-second handshake timeout SHALL retry without ARM or nonzero setpoints; invalid capabilities or leases below 200 ms SHALL fail. New attempts SHALL use different control sequences so stale ACKs cannot satisfy a later HELLO.

Connection starts disarmed
  • WHEN an operator connects to a valid target
  • THEN the client displays negotiated limits and session and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Refused or unsupported connection
  • WHEN the target returns BUSY or no valid handshake reply within one second
  • THEN the client retries with no ARM or nonzero setpoint
  • AND invalid capabilities or an unsupported lease terminate through cleanup
Old handshake cannot reconnect
  • WHEN an ACK from an earlier attempt arrives during a new handshake
  • THEN it cannot establish the new session

Link checks with disarmed recovery

The client SHALL send matched Echo every 250 ms with a 500 ms reply deadline. Missed Echo/control deadlines or socket failures SHALL clear motion, attempt bounded cleanup and retry after one second until quit. Recovery SHALL require a fresh claim and matched Echo, discard outage input, and remain disarmed until a new R and subsequent direction. Echo SHALL not prove ownership or arming. Terminal loss and scheduler failures SHALL remain fatal.

Lost link requires a new operator session
  • WHEN an Echo or ARM reply deadline expires
  • THEN the client clears intent, reports reconnecting and attempts zero/STOP/BYE
  • AND it retries HELLO with at least one second between attempts, handling quit during the wait
Recovery cannot replay buffered keys
  • GIVEN R and direction keys were received while disconnected or verifying recovery
  • WHEN a fresh claim and Echo succeed
  • THEN the client reports reconnected and remains disarmed at zero
  • AND only a new R followed by a new direction can move
Quit during outage
  • WHEN Esc, Ctrl-C or Ctrl-D is received while reconnecting
  • THEN the client attempts bounded cleanup, restores the terminal and exits without another claim

Bounded shutdown and honest reporting

Space SHALL clear motion and request STOP; quit, Ctrl-C, EOF and fatal errors SHALL exit through cleanup. Recoverable link errors SHALL clean up before retrying. Cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP and BYE within 500 ms total even if an earlier send fails. Exit SHALL restore terminal settings. Successful STOP acknowledgement SHALL require matching stopped/Stop Status. The client SHALL label unacknowledged stops and BYE as unconfirmed attempts, never verified wheel stop or release.

Cleanup tolerates a failed send
  • WHEN sending zero or STOP fails during cleanup
  • THEN BYE and terminal restoration are still attempted within the cleanup deadline

ADDED Requirements

Audible connection loss

On a connected session's first link failure the client SHALL issue one brief laptop audio alert and display loss/retry state. Repeated failures before a fresh claim and matched Echo SHALL not repeat the alert. A later outage SHALL alert again. Audio failure SHALL not prevent recovery or quit; unavailable direct audio SHALL be reported with a terminal-bell fallback. Audio playback SHALL be bounded and occur after motion is disabled.

One alert for an outage
  • WHEN a connected link fails and repeated reconnection attempts fail
  • THEN one alert is attempted for that outage
  • AND a new failure after confirmed recovery triggers a new alert
Audio unavailable
  • WHEN direct audio cannot play
  • THEN the client reports the limitation, attempts a terminal bell and continues disarmed recovery

openspec/specs/car-control-api/spec.md

car control api

car-control-api Specification

Purpose

Defines how controllers request car motion, acquire ownership, arm, stop and inspect capabilities and status consistently across the supported transports.

Requirements

Setpoint

The car's device control API SHALL accept a setpoint as a geometry_msgs/TwistStamped, using linear.x and linear.y in m/s and angular.z in rad/s, in base_link. A setpoint with any other Twist component non-zero SHALL be rejected and not applied. An owner's fresh, finite planar setpoint whose absolute linear.x, linear.y or angular.z exceeds its capability limit SHALL raise a safety stop.

Out-of-plane setpoint is rejected
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends a setpoint with linear.z = 0.1
  • THEN the setpoint is not applied and does not renew the lease
  • AND no safety stop is raised
Out-of-limits setpoint stops the car
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends a setpoint with linear.x above the capabilities' maximum
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason out-of-limits

Mecanum kinematics

The car SHALL use mecanum_drive_controller inverse kinematics and parameter names, divide wheel-speed references by configured max_wheel_speed, and clamp to −1.0..=1.0. The current geometry SHALL use radius 0.030 m and centre projection sum 0.1275 m, with zero frame offset. The profile's 40 rad/s normalization and 1/1/3 input limits are experimental values, not measured physical maxima; speed tracking is approximate (O2).

Same result as mecanum_drive_controller
  • GIVEN a wheels_radius, sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis and max_wheel_speed
  • WHEN the car is armed and applies a setpoint
  • THEN each wheel command (FL, FR, RR, RL) equals its inverse-kinematic wheel speed divided by max_wheel_speed, clamped independently to −1.0..=1.0
Same input on every source gives the same wheel commands
  • GIVEN the same setpoint
  • WHEN it is sent by an armed owner over BLE, UDP and ROS 2 in turn
  • THEN the wheel commands are identical
Combined inputs saturate independently
  • GIVEN radius 0.03 m, zero frame offset, normalization 40 rad/s and input limits allowing vx=1 and vy=1
  • WHEN the armed owner sends vx=1, vy=1, wz=0
  • THEN normalized commands are (0, 1, 0, 1), not (0, 1.667, 0, 1.667)

Open-loop motion references

Twist fields SHALL retain their standard m/s and rad/s meaning as requested motion references. Product documentation SHALL describe current open-loop tracking as approximate and link the M5 observations. The car SHALL NOT present command-derived speed as measured velocity or promise velocity accuracy without supporting evidence.

An estimate is not measured feedback
  • GIVEN the current motors have no encoders and only short-pulse observations are available
  • WHEN the product describes speed or publishes status
  • THEN observed motion estimates are identified as approximate
  • AND commanded velocity is not presented as measured feedback

Latest setpoint wins

The car SHALL apply only the owner's latest setpoint, with no queue. A setpoint whose sequence is not newer than the last accepted one SHALL NOT be applied.

Older sequence is ignored
  • GIVEN the current BLE/UDP session, or one ROS publisher, last accepted setpoint sequence 10
  • WHEN a setpoint with sequence 9 or 10 arrives
  • THEN it is not applied and does not renew the lease

Single owner

The first controller to claim SHALL become the owner. Other controllers' claims SHALL be refused and their control input ignored. Repeated UDP HELLO from the current owner SHALL return its existing session without renewing deadlines. BLE ownership SHALL disable the AP; UDP or ROS ownership SHALL stop BLE advertising. UDP and ROS share the AP and SHALL exclude one another through ownership checks, not radio shutdown.

Second claimant is refused
  • GIVEN a UDP controller owns the car
  • WHEN a second UDP controller sends a hello
  • THEN it receives BUSY
  • AND the owner is unchanged
Other radio is off while owned
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a BLE controller connects
  • THEN it becomes the owner and the car AP goes off
  • AND when ownership is released, BLE advertising and the car AP are both up
Non-owner ROS node is ignored
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 node owns the car
  • WHEN another node publishes a setpoint or an arm
  • THEN it is ignored
UDP and ROS share the Wi-Fi radio
  • GIVEN a UDP owner and a connected ROS router on the car AP
  • WHEN a ROS node sends a setpoint
  • THEN the AP stays up, the setpoint cannot claim or drive, and the UDP lease is unchanged
  • AND the same exclusion applies to UDP input while a ROS node owns the car

Claim window

If the owner sends no valid setpoint within the claim window, ownership SHALL be released.

Silent owner loses the car
  • GIVEN a controller has just claimed the car
  • WHEN the claim window passes with no valid setpoint from it
  • THEN ownership is released and every radio reopens

Explicit arming

New owners SHALL start disarmed. BLE/UDP SHALL require the owner's explicit arm and a valid lease. ROS SHALL auto-arm on an owner's valid setpoint only after a claim or lease expiry (ADR-0011). After STOP or out-of-limits, all sources SHALL require a fresh setpoint followed by explicit arm. Disarmed setpoints SHALL renew the lease while wheel commands remain zero.

Setpoints alone do not move the car
  • GIVEN a new BLE or UDP owner that has not armed
  • WHEN it streams non-zero setpoints
  • THEN every wheel command is zero
Arm without a lease is refused
  • GIVEN a new BLE or UDP owner that has sent no setpoint
  • WHEN it sends arm
  • THEN arm is refused with not-ready and the car stays disarmed
A ROS 2 stream arms the car
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a known ROS 2 node streams valid non-zero setpoints on /cmd_vel and nothing on /rovi/arm
  • THEN the first setpoint claims and arms the car and the wheel commands follow it
  • AND after a lease expiry, the resumed stream arms the car again
A ROS 2 stop stays latched while streaming
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 owner that is streaming and armed
  • WHEN it publishes /rovi/arm false and keeps streaming
  • THEN the car stops and every wheel command stays zero until the owner publishes /rovi/arm true
Arm then drive
  • GIVEN an owner with a fresh valid setpoint, a valid lease and valid motor configuration
  • WHEN it sends arm, then a non-zero setpoint
  • THEN the car is armed and the wheel commands follow the setpoint
Arm after a stop needs a new setpoint
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop while its lease was valid
  • WHEN it sends arm before any new setpoint
  • THEN arm is refused with not-ready and the car stays in safety stop
  • AND after one valid setpoint, the next arm succeeds

Lease and watchdog timeout

Only the owner's valid setpoints SHALL renew the lease. When the lease expires, the car SHALL raise a watchdog timeout and a safety stop within the lease length plus 50 ms (M8's acceptance bound), checked by the control tick independently of incoming traffic.

Silent armed owner is stopped
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN no valid setpoint arrives for longer than the lease
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason lease-expired, within the lease plus 50 ms
  • AND every wheel command is zero

Safety stop

STOP, lease expiry, owner loss and out-of-limits SHALL zero wheel commands, put both drivers in standby and disarm. Ownership SHALL be retained except on owner loss or window expiry. STOP/out-of-limits SHALL require a fresh valid setpoint then explicit ARM. Lease expiry SHALL allow ROS auto-arm on a fresh valid setpoint; BLE/UDP SHALL still require explicit ARM. Release SHALL clear session state while keeping drivers disabled.

Stop keeps the owner
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner sends stop
  • THEN the car is in safety stop with reason stop, disarmed, with every driver in standby
  • AND the controller is still the owner
Owner loss while armed
  • GIVEN the car is armed
  • WHEN the owner disconnects or sends bye
  • THEN a safety stop is raised with reason owner-lost
  • AND ownership is released
Further setpoints do not clear the latch
  • GIVEN the car stopped because of STOP or out-of-limits
  • WHEN the owner streams valid setpoints without explicit ARM
  • THEN every wheel command stays zero

Reclaim window

After a stop or an out-of-limits setpoint, the owner SHALL be kept for as long as its valid setpoints keep the lease valid. The reclaim window SHALL start when the lease lapses: at once on a lease expiry, or when the owner goes quiet after a stop or an out-of-limits setpoint. Within the window, the owner SHALL be able to resume in the same session using the explicit/automatic arming rules. When the window ends, ownership SHALL be released.

Streaming owner is kept after a stop
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop
  • WHEN it keeps streaming valid setpoints for longer than the reclaim window
  • THEN it is still the owner and the car stays in safety stop
Quiet owner after a stop is released
  • GIVEN the owner sent stop
  • WHEN it sends no setpoint after that
  • THEN the reclaim window starts when its lease lapses
  • AND ownership is released when the window ends, and every radio reopens
Out-of-limits keeps a streaming owner
  • GIVEN an out-of-limits setpoint raised a safety stop
  • WHEN the owner keeps streaming valid setpoints and then sends arm
  • THEN the car is armed in the same session
Resume within the window
  • GIVEN the car stopped on lease expiry
  • WHEN the same owner sends a valid setpoint and arm within the reclaim window
  • THEN the car is armed in the same session
Window ends
  • GIVEN the car stopped on lease expiry
  • WHEN the reclaim window passes without explicit or permitted automatic arming
  • THEN ownership is released and every radio reopens

Boot state

After power-up or reset, the car SHALL be open, with no owner, disarmed, every wheel command zero and every driver in standby.

Fresh boot
  • GIVEN the car has just booted
  • WHEN a controller reads the status
  • THEN the state is open
  • AND the car log reports every wheel command as zero

Capabilities

The car SHALL give its capabilities on every source: protocol version, wheels_radius, sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis, maximum linear.x, linear.y and angular.z, lease length, claim window and reclaim window. BLE (Capabilities characteristic) and UDP (HELLO_ACK) give them to the owner on claim; ROS 2 gives them before the claim, as below. Each value SHALL be the one the car enforces, so a controller needs no hardcoded limits.

Limits match enforcement
  • GIVEN a controller has read the capabilities
  • WHEN it sends a setpoint at exactly the maximum linear.x
  • THEN the setpoint is applied
  • AND a setpoint above it raises a safety stop
Same capabilities on every source
  • GIVEN the same car
  • WHEN a BLE, a UDP and a ROS 2 controller each read the capabilities
  • THEN every value is identical

ROS 2 capabilities topic

A ROS 2 controller claims with its first setpoint, so ROS 2 SHALL give the capabilities without a claim. The car SHALL publish them on /rovi/capabilities as std_msgs/String of space-separated key=value pairs, latched: reliable, transient local, depth 1. O9 selects this QoS or the specified volatile fallback; the published values are identical in both modes.

Late subscriber gets the capabilities
  • GIVEN the car is open and connected to the ROS 2 router
  • WHEN a node starts and subscribes to /rovi/capabilities
  • THEN it receives the capabilities without sending anything to the car
One pair per field
  • GIVEN a node has received /rovi/capabilities
  • WHEN it splits the string on spaces and =
  • THEN it gets exactly one value for every key in the capabilities encoding requirement
Reading the capabilities is not a claim
  • GIVEN the car is open
  • WHEN a ROS 2 node reads /rovi/capabilities
  • THEN the car stays open and every radio stays up

ROS 2 capabilities republish fallback

If O9 shows that zenoh-nostd cannot serve transient-local late joiners, the car SHALL use reliable, volatile, depth-1 capabilities and republish at least once per second and on every claim, release and router reconnect. Controllers SHALL subscribe with volatile durability in fallback mode. Documentation SHALL identify the chosen mode; the car SHALL NOT advertise unsupported transient-local durability.

Late subscriber gets the capabilities without latching
  • GIVEN the car uses the republish fallback
  • WHEN a node with compatible volatile QoS subscribes while the car is open and the router is healthy
  • THEN it receives the capabilities within one second

Status

The car SHALL report its status to the owner on every source (BLE Status characteristic, UDP STATUS, ROS 2 /rovi/status): state (open, claimed, armed or stopped), stop reason (none, stop, lease-expired, owner-lost or out-of-limits) and last owner control error (none, not-ready or invalid). Status SHALL be readable at once after a claim. Every status read or notification SHALL report the state at that moment.

Status follows a stop
  • GIVEN the car is armed and the owner reads status
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the next status reports safety stop with reason lease-expired
Readable right after the claim
  • GIVEN a BLE controller has just connected
  • WHEN it reads Status before any other write
  • THEN the status reports claimed with no error

ROS 2 status topic

The car SHALL publish /rovi/status as std_msgs/String of space-separated key=value pairs with the same content as the other sources' status: state (open, claimed, armed or stopped), reason (none except while stopped), error (none when clear) and session (decimal u32, 0 while open). It SHALL publish on every change of any of these and at least once a second, so a late subscriber sees the current status within a second.

Stop reason on ROS 2
  • GIVEN the car is armed under a ROS 2 owner
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the next /rovi/status has state=stopped and reason=lease-expired
Refused arm on ROS 2
  • GIVEN a ROS 2 owner stopped by its own STOP
  • WHEN it publishes arm before any new setpoint
  • THEN the next /rovi/status has state=stopped and error=not-ready
Status on a change
  • GIVEN a node subscribed to /rovi/status
  • WHEN the state changes
  • THEN it receives the new status without waiting for the next periodic publish

Last command error

On every source, a refused owner control command (ARM/STOP; not-ready or invalid) SHALL persist as the last error until the owner's next successful control command. Setpoints and echo SHALL NOT clear it. New sessions SHALL start with no error. Non-owner or old-session input SHALL NOT change it. BUSY is a response to a claimant, not an owner-status error.

Refused arm shows on every source
  • GIVEN a BLE, UDP or ROS owner that sent STOP and has sent no valid setpoint since
  • WHEN it sends explicit ARM
  • THEN the status reports the last command error not-ready
  • AND a later setpoint does not clear it, and a successful arm does
Non-owner commands do not change the owner's status
  • GIVEN an owner whose status reports no error
  • WHEN another controller sends arm
  • THEN the owner's status still reports no error

Input validation before state changes

Malformed framing/CDR, non-finite Twist components, non-planar Twist, invalid Bool/control payloads, and unknown ROS publishers SHALL NOT claim, renew a lease, change outputs or consume a setpoint sequence. An identifiable owner's invalid control payload SHALL report invalid; invalid setpoint/framing SHALL be discarded. Owner/session and sequence checks SHALL precede limit enforcement, so an intruder or stale packet cannot stop the car.

Invalid setpoint leaves the stream intact
  • GIVEN an armed owner with last sequence 10
  • WHEN sequence 11 contains NaN or truncated CDR
  • THEN the previous output and lease deadline stay unchanged
  • AND a later valid sequence 11 can be accepted
Stale or non-owner oversized input cannot stop the owner
  • GIVEN an armed owner with last sequence 10
  • WHEN sequence 9 from that owner, or input from a non-owner, exceeds a velocity limit
  • THEN it is ignored without changing the state or renewing the lease
Bad first ROS input does not claim
  • GIVEN the car is open and a known ROS publisher
  • WHEN it sends a non-finite or out-of-limits setpoint
  • THEN the car stays open and disabled

Setpoint frame and time interpretation

Empty frame_id SHALL mean base_link; base_link SHALL be accepted. Other frame names SHALL be rejected because the car does not transform frames. CDR strings SHALL be valid UTF-8, NUL-terminated and at most 64 bytes excluding the terminator. Receive time SHALL govern leases; the header stamp SHALL NOT substitute for a synchronized clock. A timestamp with nanoseconds outside 0..999999999 SHALL be rejected.

Unsupported frame does not drive
  • GIVEN an armed owner
  • WHEN it sends an otherwise valid twist in map
  • THEN the sample is discarded without lease renewal or sequence consumption
Unsynchronized stamp is not a freshness clock
  • GIVEN a valid owner and a newer setpoint sequence
  • WHEN a supported-frame setpoint arrives with an old or zero header timestamp
  • THEN it is accepted using the local receive time for its lease

Sequence domains

BLE/UDP setpoint sequences SHALL use u32 serial ordering: newer iff wrapping difference is in 1..2^31-1; equal and exactly-half-range values SHALL be dropped. ROS SHALL compare full nonnegative i64 attachment sequences strictly increasingly per publisher GID, independently for setpoint and arm publishers. Sequence history SHALL reset with the session; accepted messages from distinct owner publishers SHALL be ordered by receipt, never by comparing their counters.

BLE or UDP counter wraps
  • GIVEN last setpoint sequence 4294967295
  • WHEN sequence 0 arrives in the same session
  • THEN it is newer; a subsequent 4294967295 is stale
Same-node publishers have independent counters
  • GIVEN an owner node with setpoint publisher A at sequence 100 and publisher B with no accepted sample
  • WHEN B sends sequence 1, then A repeats sequence 100
  • THEN B's setpoint is accepted and A's duplicate is dropped
  • AND an arm publisher's own sequence 1 is not compared with either setpoint counter

Session isolation and ROS identity

UDP identity SHALL include peer address/port and the current session ID; BLE identity SHALL include the connection lifetime, not a reusable handle alone. ROS ownership SHALL use graph-announced node identity (zid/nid), not publisher GID; unknown publishers SHALL be ignored. Release or adapter reconnect SHALL discard its queued old-generation input and ordering state. Stale UDP session IDs and callbacks from closed BLE connections SHALL be ignored.

Old UDP traffic cannot affect a new claim
  • GIVEN the same peer has released session S and claimed session T
  • WHEN a delayed ARM, STOP or setpoint with session S arrives
  • THEN ownership, state, lease and last error for T remain unchanged
An arm publisher belongs to the owning node
  • GIVEN cmd_vel and arm publishers announced under one node, with distinct GIDs
  • WHEN that node owns the car and sends a valid explicit ARM with a fresh lease
  • THEN ARM succeeds; an unannounced publisher or another node cannot arm it
Router disconnect ends an owning ROS session
  • GIVEN a ROS owner and queued adapter input
  • WHEN the adapter detects router disconnection
  • THEN owner loss stops and releases the car, old queued input is discarded, and reconnect re-declares endpoints and rebuilds graph identity
  • AND before disconnection is detected, missing setpoints still trigger the independent lease timeout

Motor validation fault integration

A motor-layer validation fault SHALL cause a device out-of-limits safety stop and a diagnostic identifying the internal wheel fault. Both drivers SHALL remain in standby until the owner sends a fresh valid setpoint followed by explicit ARM, on every source including ROS. Repeated control ticks or new valid setpoints alone SHALL NOT re-enable motor control. Invalid boot configuration SHALL prevent motor enable and make ARM fail not-ready.

Internal wheel fault cannot auto-recover
  • GIVEN an armed ROS owner and a fault injected into one computed wheel command
  • WHEN motor control reports the fault
  • THEN the car reports stopped/out-of-limits and both drivers stay disabled
  • AND continued setpoints alone do not resume; a fresh valid setpoint then explicit ARM can recover with a valid configuration

Capabilities encoding

ROS capabilities SHALL contain the nine keys in the scenario below exactly once, with space-separated key=value tokens and locale-independent decimal numbers. Geometry and input limits SHALL describe the same canonical f32 values encoded by BLE/UDP; integer fields SHALL be exact. Field order SHALL be insignificant. A session ID SHALL NOT be a capability; UDP carries it in the frame header.

Keys and units are unambiguous
  • GIVEN a capabilities message
  • WHEN a controller parses it
  • THEN version is an integer protocol version; wheels_radius and sum_of_robot_center_projection_on_X_Y_axis are metres
  • AND max_vx and max_vy are m/s, max_wz is rad/s
  • AND lease_ms, claim_ms, reclaim_ms are integer milliseconds
  • AND floats use enough digits to round-trip their canonical f32 values

Status delivery and empty values

BLE SHALL update readable Status immediately on claim and every change, and notify subscribed centrals on changes. UDP SHALL reply STATUS to owner ARM/STOP, including refusals, and send STATUS on a stop transition to its owner; it provides no reliable delivery guarantee. ROS SHALL emit all four status keys on each publication, with reason=none outside stopped and error=none when clear. Release SHALL clear the status reason/error and report open.

Release does not leave a stale reason
  • GIVEN a stopped owner with reason stop and error not-ready
  • WHEN ownership is released
  • THEN readable/published status is open with no reason or error and ROS session=0
  • AND the next claimant starts with no previous-session error

Valid operating profile

Geometry and normalization SHALL be finite and positive; frame offsets SHALL be finite. Input limits SHALL be finite nonnegative f32-representable values, enforced after canonicalizing to the advertised f32 values. Lease and window lengths SHALL be integers in 1..65535 ms. Invalid profiles SHALL fail initialization with drivers disabled rather than advertise truncated values or permit claims. Numerical overflow during valid-input kinematics SHALL trigger motor fault handling.

Invalid normalization fails closed
  • GIVEN max_wheel_speed is zero or NaN, or a lease exceeds 65535 ms
  • WHEN the device initializes
  • THEN initialization reports an error, motor enable is unavailable and control claims are not accepted

Deadline ordering

Before processing control input at time t, the device SHALL process any claim, lease or reclaim deadline at or before t using a monotonic clock. Expired sessions SHALL NOT be revived by queued ARM or setpoint input. After release, BLE/UDP SHALL require a new claim; ROS MAY create a new claim from an otherwise valid sample. Automatic ROS arming SHALL NOT clear an existing STOP/out-of-limits latch before release.

Packet on the reclaim boundary
  • GIVEN a UDP session with reclaim deadline t
  • WHEN its ARM or setpoint arrives at t
  • THEN the old ownership is released first, and that packet cannot drive or renew the expired session

Echo is observational

UDP Echo and the BLE Echo characteristic SHALL return payloads of at most 32 bytes unchanged and discard larger ones. Echo SHALL NOT claim, arm, change wheel commands, renew deadlines, consume setpoint sequences or clear errors. UDP echo SHALL be available to non-owners; BLE connection itself still claims as usual, so BLE echo does not provide a parallel non-owner connection.

Echo does not keep an owner alive
  • GIVEN an owner stops sending setpoints but continues echo probes
  • WHEN the lease expires
  • THEN the normal lease stop occurs and ownership eventually expires without ARM

New session allocation

Each new claim SHALL allocate a nonzero session ID; repeated HELLO by the current UDP owner SHALL keep that ID and its deadlines. UDP IDs SHALL be seeded randomly per boot and incremented per new claim, skipping zero on wrap. This SHALL be documented as stale-packet separation, not authentication or a guarantee against deliberate replay. BLE sessions SHALL use connection generations; ROS sessions SHALL use the identity and queue rules above.

Repeated hello does not reset a claim
  • GIVEN a UDP owner in session S with an existing claim or lease deadline
  • WHEN the same peer repeats HELLO
  • THEN HELLO_ACK carries S and the same capabilities, without extending either deadline

Bounded ROS ordering history

The adapter SHALL retain sequence high-water marks for every accepted owner publisher for the current session, including across publisher removal. Other graph announcements SHALL NOT evict those marks. If bounded storage cannot track another owner publisher, its input SHALL be discarded without lease renewal rather than accepted without replay checks. Ownership release SHALL clear these session marks.

Unrelated publishers cannot reset ordering
  • GIVEN an owner publisher whose last accepted sequence is 100
  • WHEN unrelated graph announcements fill the table and that publisher repeats sequence 99
  • THEN sequence 99 is rejected and cannot renew the lease
