openspec/specs/iphone-ble-teleoperation/spec.md

iphone ble teleoperation

iphone-ble-teleoperation Specification

Purpose

Lets an iPhone user control the normal product car over its existing BLE API with explicit arming, bounded touch intent and visible limits on connection and physical-state evidence.

Requirements

Supported web delivery

The controller SHALL run as an HTTPS page with Bluefy as its supported iPhone BLE host. It SHALL check the picker API before selection and required GATT read/notify and explicit write modes before writes; missing support SHALL disable control with an explanation. Buttons SHALL be the default; only a user selection of Physical mode or explicit sensor retry may request sensor permission. Published assets SHALL contain no secrets or third-party runtime scripts.

Unsupported host
  • WHEN the page opens without required Web Bluetooth APIs, including in an unsupported Safari session, or without HTTPS
  • THEN it explains that supported Bluefy/HTTPS is required and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoints

Explicit discovery and selection

The client SHALL invoke the browser device picker only from an explicit Choose & Connect action while active. It SHALL select the existing name-only advertisement without requiring an advertised service UUID, request access to the product service, and connect only to the chosen device. The picker SHALL NOT be described as a claim; GATT connection is the claim. Cancellation/no result SHALL NOT be described as proof that the car is busy.

Browser selection precedes connection
  • WHEN Choose & Connect opens the browser picker, including when same-name candidates exist
  • THEN no GATT connection occurs until the user selects a candidate, and the page does not auto-select a remembered device
  • AND the action explains that connecting claims the car and switches off its Wi-Fi AP; the page does not promise picker RSSI or distinguishable hardware addresses
Picker cancelled or completed after local cancellation
  • WHEN the picker is cancelled, has no selection, or returns after the local attempt was cancelled
  • THEN no connection is started; a new manual action is required
  • AND the page does not claim it can impose a scan timeout or forcibly dismiss the browser picker

Validate the connected car

Setup SHALL start locally disarmed at zero. Before regular streaming, the client SHALL validate GATT properties, 27-byte version-1 capabilities, positive finite geometry, finite nonnegative limits, nonzero windows, lease >=500 ms, claim >=1000 ms, valid Claimed/Stopped Status and an initial 72-byte zero write submission. Setup SHALL finish within 10 seconds of GATT connect invocation or end through cleanup. It SHALL send no ARM or nonzero setpoint.

Unsupported payload or capabilities
  • WHEN required characteristics/properties or capabilities are invalid, windows are unsupported, or the initial 72-byte submission is rejected
  • THEN the client reports incompatibility and attempts disconnect without fragmentation, protocol substitution or automatic reconnect
  • AND a resolved without-response write is not displayed as proof of device receipt or measured MTU
Claim expires during setup
  • WHEN discovery/subscription takes longer than the car's claim window and the car releases the connection
  • THEN setup fails without automatic reconnect, even if the local 10-second deadline has not passed

Existing BLE wire contract

The client SHALL use the existing product UUIDs and write each setpoint as one 72-byte value: little-endian u32 sequence plus 68-byte little-endian TwistStamped CDR, empty frame, zero timestamp, and only vx/vy/wz nonzero. Sequences SHALL advance with wrapping u32 ordering per connection. ARM/STOP SHALL use one-byte values 1/2 with response. BLE SHALL have no UDP header, numeric session ID, HELLO or BYE.

Wire values agree with the product
  • WHEN zero, each direction and a sequence wrapping from 4294967295 to 0 are encoded
  • THEN bytes match the existing Rust/Python product vectors and the unused Twist fields are zero
  • AND a new connection starts a new sequence history

Explicit zero then ARM

ARM SHALL require a new user action; Physical ARM SHALL capture neutral from fresh valid sensors in that action. It SHALL invalidate touches, stream fresh zero and send ARM once. Local motion permission SHALL require the ARM write and a subsequent fresh Status read reporting Armed/none/none within one second. A notification alone SHALL NOT grant motion. Failure, refusal or timeout SHALL clear intent and end through cleanup; late callbacks SHALL NOT arm locally.

Touch predates ARM
  • GIVEN a direction is held while locally disarmed
  • WHEN ARM succeeds
  • THEN only zero is sent until that touch is released and a new direction press begins
ARM is refused or its confirmation is late
  • WHEN ARM returns an ATT error or its write/Status confirmation misses the one-second deadline
  • THEN the client remains locally disarmed and requires a new connection and explicit ARM before motion
One explicit Physical action captures neutral and arms
  • WHEN sensors are enabled while disarmed
  • THEN no ARM or nonzero setpoint is sent
  • AND a subsequent explicit Set neutral & ARM captures the current fresh screen-up pose without a separate calibration tap, sends zero then ARM and requires a separate post-arm START action
  • AND missing/stale/invalid sensors or an invalid neutral posture refuse ARM locally without an ARM write

Gentle input modes

Buttons SHALL retain six single-axis hold directions; multiple touches yield zero until all release and a new press. Physical mode SHALL combine calibrated forward/back tilt as vx, side tilt as vy and heading offset as wz. Each axis SHALL remain within min(0.1 m/s, advertised translation maximum) or min(0.3 rad/s, advertised rotation maximum). Zero-limit axes SHALL stay zero; button velocities SHALL NOT combine.

Direction mapping respects limits
  • WHEN each direction is held after successful ARM
  • THEN forward/back use +/-vx, left/right +/-vy, counter-clockwise/clockwise +/-wz, with other fields zero and advertised limits respected
  • AND max_vx=0.05 yields forward vx=0.05, while max_vy=0 disables both strafe controls
Physical movement combines without exceeding per-axis limits
  • WHEN explicitly started Physical control supplies forward, left and counter-clockwise offsets after successful ARM
  • THEN vx, vy and wz may be positive together, each within its gentle and advertised maximum
  • AND a zero advertised axis stays zero without disabling other permitted components

Hold cancellation and input expiry

Buttons nonzero intent SHALL require one tracked press inside a direction control while active and locally armed. Release, bounds exit, cancellation, lost tracking or multiple touches SHALL clear intent before the next send. Only UI renewal may extend the 250 ms monotonic hold deadline. Buttons retain arm after expiry and require a new press. Physical control SHALL use the explicit START/PAUSE gate and independent foreground renewal deadline instead of a held pointer.

Finger release or missing renewals
  • WHEN a held direction ends, is cancelled, slides outside, or has no renewal for 250 ms
  • THEN the next setpoint is zero and no buffered motion is played back
  • AND sliding back inside does not resume motion without a new press

Periodic latest-intent stream

After setup the client SHALL attempt one latest setpoint every 50 ms, zero when locally disarmed, awaiting ARM, without a valid Buttons hold or while Physical control is paused. It SHALL check lifecycle/stops/expiry before sending, allow one pending setpoint write and retain no motion backlog. A scheduler gap or interval without submission of >=200 ms SHALL revoke local arm and end through cleanup, without catch-up motion. Write rejection SHALL end the session.

Transport backpressure
  • GIVEN nonzero intent and a pending write prevents another submission
  • WHEN that procedure completes before the 200 ms failure bound
  • THEN the next send uses only current unexpired intent, with no accumulated writes
  • AND completion at or after the bound cannot resume motion; a promise resolving does not confirm applied wheel motion

Validate Status and link health

The client SHALL validate three-byte Status codes and state/reason consistency, subscribe to changes and schedule a Status read every 500 ms while ready, with at most one transaction pending. A transaction taking >=1000 ms, malformed Status, GATT error, Open Status or unexpected Armed Status SHALL revoke local motion and end through cleanup. Stopped Status SHALL revoke local arm. Callbacks from old connections or cancelled operations SHALL NOT change the current session.

Silence and old callbacks
  • WHEN Status is unchanged without notifications
  • THEN reads refresh its observation age; missing a read deadline ends the session
  • AND an Armed callback from an earlier connection cannot authorize a newly connected session

STOP and re-arm latch

STOP SHALL remain available throughout a connected session, clear intent immediately and request Control=2 with response. It SHALL override ARM and touch input. Confirmation SHALL require successful STOP write completion and a subsequent fresh Stopped/Stop/none Status read within one second. Confirmed STOP or reported safety stop SHALL require explicit ARM and a new press before motion; unconfirmed STOP SHALL end through cleanup. Zero alone SHALL NOT be described as STOP.

STOP races with ARM and touch
  • WHEN STOP occurs while ARM is pending or direction events are queued
  • THEN pending local arming is invalidated, queued direction input is discarded, and any late Armed result cannot enable motion
  • AND after confirmed STOP the client may keep streaming zero to retain ownership until manual re-arm or Disconnect

Active foreground and manual recovery

During a connected session, blur/hidden/pagehide, host inactivity, observed permission/service loss or Bluetooth failure SHALL clear holds, revoke local arm and end through cleanup. Return/reload/restoration SHALL require manual Choose & Connect and ARM, never automatic recovery/replay. A pending picker SHALL NOT connect while inactive. If inactive UI stops renewing input, expiry SHALL clear motion even while transmission runs. Sustained inactive motion SHALL fail host acceptance.

Lock or Bluetooth loss while holding
  • WHEN the phone locks, changes app, or loses Bluetooth while a direction is held
  • THEN observed inactivity/loss clears motion before another send, and foreground return cannot resume the hold
  • AND if execution or UI renewal stops without an event, input expiry or the independent firmware lease stops motion; runnable cleanup is not promised after suspension/termination
  • AND phone checks must reject a host that keeps renewing nonzero motion while inactive

Bounded best-effort shutdown

Disconnect, setup failure, interruption and handled failure SHALL clear intent and stop normal writes, then independently attempt zero and STOP where supported, and local cancellation, within 500 ms total while runnable. Cancellation SHALL still be attempted if a write fails or never completes. The UI SHALL distinguish attempted, device-reported STOP and local disconnect; it SHALL NOT infer physical wheel stop or immediate ownership release from a write or cancellation.

Shutdown cannot complete its writes
  • WHEN zero is blocked or STOP receives no completion
  • THEN local cancellation is requested by the shared 500 ms deadline without waiting indefinitely
  • AND late callbacks are ignored and stop/release remain unconfirmed

Visible state and evidence limits

The UI SHALL show selected device name/available ID, phase, local arm, limits, packet size, requested vx/vy/wz and reported state/reason/error with age. Unexposed MTU/capacity SHALL be labelled unavailable. Controls SHALL have text/accessibility labels, adequate targets and cues beyond color. Buttons accessibility activation SHALL NOT latch motion; explicit Physical START/PAUSE activation SHALL match a tap. Docs SHALL separate approximate references, host tests, phone/radio and wheel evidence.

Reported Armed does not mean moving wheels
  • WHEN reported Status is Armed but no button direction is held and Physical control is paused, or interruption revoked local permission
  • THEN requested motion is zero, Status retains its observation age, and the UI does not claim measured speed, live wheel state or certified emergency stopping

Visible control status

Local arm state, STOP, Physical START/PAUSE, requested motion and the latest session message SHALL remain visible while scrolling, including after fault disconnect. Physical mode SHALL show running/paused state and explain unavailable input. Scroll SHALL clear button holds and pause Physical control before another send, preserving arm/neutral. Real lifecycle and stream failures SHALL retain cleanup. Posture faults SHALL identify the angle, observed value and limit.

Scroll while armed at zero
  • WHEN the user scrolls while Physical control is paused
  • THEN arm state, STOP and the session reason stay visible, intent remains zero and scrolling alone does not disconnect
  • AND a genuine stream or lifecycle failure still disarms and displays its reason

Explicit physical sensor setup

Physical sensor setup SHALL begin only from an active user selection of Physical mode or explicit Retry action, with feature detection and permission handling. Missing/denied/failed permission or missing finite alpha/beta/gamma SHALL prevent physical motion. Late permission results or callbacks from an earlier mode, enable attempt or closed session SHALL NOT change current input. Sensor events SHALL NOT select a device, ARM or write BLE.

Denial and delayed permission response
  • WHEN permission is denied or resolves after switching to Buttons or leaving the page
  • THEN no Physical running state or calibration becomes valid and no automatic connection or ARM occurs
  • AND Buttons remain available without sensor permission

Physical calibration and angle mapping

Each explicit Physical ARM SHALL calibrate fresh finite orientation while locally disarmed with no pending control. Neutral beta/gamma SHALL be within ±30° with screen up. Shortest offsets SHALL map negative beta to forward, negative gamma to left strafe, positive alpha to left rotation, with 3° dead zones and linear scale to saturation at 20°. Held heading offset SHALL sustain rotation; neutral SHALL request zero. No silent recentering is allowed.

Heading wrap and sustained twist
  • WHEN calibrated alpha is 350° and current alpha is 10° while Physical control is explicitly running
  • THEN the heading offset is +20°, requesting capped positive wz rather than a −340° turn
  • AND fresh unchanged samples sustain that request, returning to neutral zeros it, and gyro rotation rate is not integrated
Neutral posture and operating envelope
  • WHEN calibration beta or gamma exceeds ±30°, or running Physical control has current beta/gamma beyond ±60° or heading offset beyond ±90°, or the screen orientation changes
  • THEN calibration or motion is rejected with an explanation
  • AND an armed or arming Physical session loses calibration and ends through cleanup, with manual recovery required
Reading posture while paused
  • WHEN Physical control is paused and the phone leaves the operating envelope
  • THEN intent remains zero and START is unavailable, preserving arm and neutral
  • AND returning to valid fresh input permits only a new explicit START at neutral; it neither recenters nor resumes driving

Independent physical sample freshness

Only new valid orientation events SHALL renew a 250 ms monotonic sample deadline. Expiry during running Physical control SHALL be checked before replacing a sample and end through cleanup before another nonzero send. Paused gaps SHALL preserve arm/neutral at zero and reject START until fresh input returns. Invalid input or changed reference SHALL revoke calibration and end armed/arming sessions. UI frames, stream ticks and cached values SHALL NOT renew samples or restart driving.

Sensor stops while UI and stream continue
  • WHEN no valid orientation arrives for 250 ms while Physical control and the transmitter continue running
  • THEN requested motion becomes zero, calibration and local arm are revoked, and cleanup begins
  • AND a late sample or resumed UI cannot restore motion without manual recovery
Sensor pause while paused
  • WHEN orientation pauses with Physical control paused, but the foreground and BLE stream remain healthy
  • THEN no motion is permitted until new valid input returns, while arm and neutral remain
  • AND an attempted START during the pause cannot start motion when readings return; a new explicit START at neutral is required

Explicit control mode switching

The same client SHALL expose Buttons and Physical modes, default Buttons without persistence. Every actual mode change SHALL clear both inputs and calibration, disable sensor collection and revoke local arm. A ready session SHALL supersede pending ARM with STOP; setup/picker attempts SHALL be cancelled. New mode selection SHALL NOT ARM or restore a hold; fresh prerequisites, ARM and post-arm input action are required.

Switch while Physical is running or ARM is pending
  • WHEN the user changes modes while Physical control is running or awaiting ARM completion
  • THEN no later old running state, sample or ARM result can authorize motion in the new mode
  • AND a ready connection may remain at zero after confirmed STOP until a fresh explicit ARM

Tap-based Physical driving

Physical control SHALL stay paused after ARM. START SHALL require active foreground, confirmed arm, fresh calibration and three offsets within ±3°. Running needs no held touch. PAUSE/scroll SHALL clear intent before the next send, retaining arm/neutral. ARM, STOP, mode changes and cleanup SHALL clear running state. Only UI frames may renew its 250 ms deadline; expiry SHALL revoke calibration and end through cleanup. Only a new explicit START may restart it.

Start, tilt and pause without holding
  • WHEN the user taps START at neutral after ARM, releases the screen and tilts the phone
  • THEN fresh input supplies bounded motion without a held pointer and the persistent control reads PAUSE
  • AND PAUSE yields zero while retaining local arm and neutral; returning sensor data or neutral alone does not restart driving
Neutral and explicit restart are required
  • WHEN START occurs before ARM confirmation, while sensors are stale, or outside ±3° of calibrated neutral
  • THEN no running state or nonzero intent is granted, and later data/ARM completion cannot replay that START
  • AND after pause/scroll or a new ARM, motion requires a new explicit START at neutral
Foreground renewal stops independently of sensors
  • WHEN Physical control is running and no UI frame renews its deadline for 250 ms while fresh sensors and the stream continue
  • THEN intent becomes zero and local arm/calibration are revoked through cleanup
  • AND resumed frames and samples cannot restart driving or reconnect

Mobile controller layout

The controller SHALL present labelled Buttons/Physical segmented radios, requested motion and connection/arm/driving states. At 320×568 through 390×844 CSS pixels, six Buttons directions and requested motion SHALL fit above a persistent thumb-reachable ARM/START/PAUSE and STOP dock. Sensor setup SHALL be implicit in choosing Physical; Retry appears only when needed. Protocol/raw sensor details SHALL be collapsed by default; opening diagnostics SHALL clear input without ARM or restart.

Drive without scrolling through setup details
  • WHEN the connected controller is viewed in either mode on the supported portrait sizes
  • THEN the current primary action and STOP remain visible, and requested motion is readable without opening diagnostics
  • AND Buttons keeps held directions while Physical keeps explicit neutral-gated START/PAUSE; choosing modes still disarms
Larger text and keyboard access
  • WHEN text is enlarged to 200%, a keyboard selects modes, or a narrow/landscape viewport is used
  • THEN controls remain labelled, targets at least 44×44 CSS pixels, content can scroll without horizontal overflow and focus is not covered by the dock
  • AND light/dark themes have readable text, motion is reduced when requested and no sensor or Bluetooth permission is requested by initial page load
Diagnostics while Physical is running
  • WHEN connection diagnostics are opened during Physical driving
  • THEN input becomes zero and stays paused without losing neutral/arm or disconnecting solely because details opened
  • AND closing details or returning readings cannot resume driving; a new explicit START at neutral is needed

openspec/specs/laptop-teleoperation/spec.md

laptop teleoperation

laptop-teleoperation Specification

Purpose

Lets a laptop operator control the existing car UDP API interactively with explicit arming, bounded motion input, visible state and predictable failure cleanup.

Requirements

Explicit connection without motion

The client SHALL require an interactive terminal and exactly one transport: explicit UDP IPv4:port or BLE discovery with optional MAC. Each UDP attempt SHALL validate HELLO's nonzero session/capabilities and use fresh control sequences. BLE SHALL validate GATT/capabilities before controls. All connections SHALL start disarmed at zero. BUSY/unavailable targets SHALL retry without motion; invalid capabilities or leases below 200 ms SHALL fail.

Connection starts disarmed
  • WHEN an operator connects to a valid UDP or BLE target
  • THEN the client displays negotiated limits and connection identity and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Refused or unsupported connection
  • WHEN UDP returns BUSY, its one-second handshake expires, or BLE discovery/connect fails
  • THEN the client retries with no ARM or nonzero setpoint
  • AND invalid capabilities or an unsupported lease terminate through cleanup
Old handshake cannot reconnect
  • WHEN a UDP ACK from an earlier attempt arrives during a new handshake
  • THEN it cannot establish the new session

Explicit arm and stop latch

Only an operator R key SHALL request ARM, after clearing motion and sending a fresh zero setpoint. Motion SHALL remain disabled until a matching successful Armed Status reply arrives. A refused/timed-out ARM, STOP or reported safety stop SHALL clear intent and require a new R key before further motion. Held or repeated motion keys SHALL never arm the car.

Keys cannot arm
  • GIVEN a connected but locally disarmed client
  • WHEN motion keys arrive
  • THEN no nonzero setpoint is sent
Arm does not replay a direction
  • GIVEN previous motion intent exists
  • WHEN R is pressed and ARM succeeds
  • THEN the client starts armed at zero and requires a subsequent motion key

Gentle planar directions

W/S SHALL request forward/backward, A/D left/right strafe, and Q/E counter-clockwise/clockwise rotation in base_link. Only one direction SHALL be active at a time. Translation magnitude SHALL be min(0.1 m/s, the advertised axis maximum), rotation min(0.3 rad/s, advertised maximum). Disabled axes SHALL remain zero. Other Twist components SHALL be zero; simultaneous keys SHALL not combine velocities.

Limits below the defaults are respected
  • GIVEN an armed client whose advertised max_vx is 0.05 m/s
  • WHEN W is received
  • THEN vx is 0.05 and vy/wz are zero
New direction replaces the previous one
  • GIVEN W was the current direction
  • WHEN E is received
  • THEN vx/vy become zero and only clockwise wz is requested

Input expiry and latest intent

Each recognized motion key SHALL expire 250 ms after its monotonic receipt time. The next send after expiry SHALL be zero. Key repeats SHALL refresh that window; unrelated keys SHALL not. Buffered motion SHALL not form a playback queue. STOP, quit, disarm and failure SHALL clear buffered motion. The client SHALL describe key repeat as renewal, not claim it receives physical key-release events.

Motion input expires
  • GIVEN W was received at t and no subsequent motion key arrives
  • WHEN a send occurs at or after t+250 ms
  • THEN the transmitted setpoint is zero
Stop wins over buffered movement
  • WHEN a read batch contains movement and Space or quit
  • THEN movement is discarded and no later queued key replays it

Periodic stream and scheduling failure

While connected, the client SHALL send the current zero or armed intent every 50 ms with wrapping u32 setpoint sequences. It SHALL process received stops and input expiry before each send. A send-loop gap of at least 200 ms SHALL clear intent and end the run through cleanup; catching up SHALL not send a backlog of motion. Host scheduling SHALL not be described as a guaranteed physical stopping bound.

Delayed loop cannot replay motion
  • GIVEN nonzero intent and a 200 ms gap since the last send-loop iteration
  • WHEN the client resumes
  • THEN it sends no further nonzero setpoint and enters cleanup

Validate and correlate device input

The client SHALL validate device payload lengths and codes. UDP replies SHALL match the selected endpoint, version and current session, with Status matching a pending control sequence or unsolicited zero. BLE input SHALL belong to the current connection generation and its native GATT operation. Wrong-peer, malformed, stale or unmatched input SHALL not authorize motion or extend deadlines. Unsolicited stopped Status SHALL disable local motion before the next send.

Queued notification precedes an ARM reply
  • WHEN a stopped notification arrives before the matching ARM reply/readback
  • THEN the client clears motion and does not confuse the notification with successful ARM
Intruder packet cannot enable movement
  • WHEN another endpoint, session or closed BLE connection sends Armed Status
  • THEN local arming remains unchanged

Link checks with disarmed recovery

The client SHALL send matched Echo every 250 ms with a 500 ms reply deadline. Missed Echo/control deadlines or socket failures SHALL clear motion, attempt bounded cleanup and retry after one second until quit. Recovery SHALL require a fresh claim and matched Echo, discard outage input, and remain disarmed until a new R and subsequent direction. Echo SHALL not prove ownership or arming. Terminal loss and scheduler failures SHALL remain fatal.

Lost link requires a new operator session
  • WHEN an Echo or ARM reply deadline expires
  • THEN the client clears intent, reports reconnecting and attempts zero/STOP/BYE
  • AND it retries HELLO with at least one second between attempts, handling quit during the wait
Recovery cannot replay buffered keys
  • GIVEN R and direction keys were received while disconnected or verifying recovery
  • WHEN a fresh claim and Echo succeed
  • THEN the client reports reconnected and remains disarmed at zero
  • AND only a new R followed by a new direction can move
Quit during outage
  • WHEN Esc, Ctrl-C or Ctrl-D is received while reconnecting
  • THEN the client attempts bounded cleanup, restores the terminal and exits without another claim

Bounded shutdown and honest reporting

Space SHALL clear motion and request STOP; quit, Ctrl-C, EOF and fatal errors SHALL exit through cleanup. Recoverable link errors SHALL clean up before retrying. UDP cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP and BYE within 500 ms total even if an earlier send fails. Exit SHALL restore terminal settings. Matching stopped/Stop Status SHALL be required for STOP acknowledgement. Unacknowledged STOP and BYE SHALL be labelled attempts, never verified wheel stop or release.

Cleanup tolerates a failed send
  • WHEN sending zero or STOP fails during UDP cleanup
  • THEN BYE and terminal restoration are still attempted within the cleanup deadline

Observable commands and evidence limits

The client SHALL show connection/local-arm state, UDP session or BLE connection generation, last valid device Status/reply age and requested vx/vy/wz. Last-reported Status SHALL be distinguished from live physical state; Echo SHALL not refresh Status age. Documentation SHALL identify open-loop speeds as approximate and cleanup as best effort. Simulator/fake-GATT passes SHALL not count as wheel, radio or electrical acceptance.

A responsive rebooted device does not prove ownership
  • GIVEN a UDP car reboots and answers Echo but does not accept the old session
  • WHEN the client displays its state
  • THEN it shows Status as last reported with its original age, sends no new HELLO merely because Echo replies, and does not claim ownership recovery

Audible connection loss

On a connected session's first link failure the client SHALL issue one brief laptop audio alert and display loss/retry state. Repeated failures before a fresh claim and matched Echo SHALL not repeat the alert. A later outage SHALL alert again. Audio failure SHALL not prevent recovery or quit; unavailable direct audio SHALL be reported with a terminal-bell fallback. Audio playback SHALL be bounded and occur after motion is disabled.

One alert for an outage
  • WHEN a connected link fails and repeated reconnection attempts fail
  • THEN one alert is attempted for that outage
  • AND a new failure after confirmed recovery triggers a new alert
Audio unavailable
  • WHEN direct audio cannot play
  • THEN the client reports the limitation, attempts a terminal bell and continues disarmed recovery

BLE target and GATT validation

BLE SHALL discover/connect within five seconds each, select one advertising Rovi M8 or an explicit MAC, and pin that address for retries. Ambiguous names SHALL fail. Before controls it SHALL validate the car service, characteristic properties, capabilities and 72-byte write-without-response capacity (ATT MTU at least 75). Incompatible GATT SHALL fail closed.

Unsafe or ambiguous peer cannot move
  • WHEN discovery is ambiguous, the service is missing, or setpoint capacity is below 72 bytes
  • THEN the client reports the limitation, disconnects any connection and sends no ARM or nonzero setpoint
Name discovery pins the device for recovery
  • GIVEN name discovery selected one device
  • WHEN its connection drops and another Rovi M8 advertises
  • THEN retries target the original device's MAC and cannot roam to the other car

BLE control confirmation and callback lifetime

BLE SHALL use native u32-sequenced setpoints and ARM/STOP bytes. ARM SHALL send zero first, succeed at ATT level and obtain fresh Armed/clear Status before enabling local motion. Notifications alone SHALL not authorize ARM. STOP, a safety notification or newer intent SHALL invalidate a pending ARM confirmation. Callbacks/Echo from an earlier connection generation SHALL not affect current state. Malformed Status SHALL not authorize motion.

Stop wins over an in-flight ARM
  • WHEN Space or a safety stop arrives while an ARM write/readback is pending
  • THEN the eventual Armed readback cannot re-enable local motion
Closed connection callback arrives late
  • WHEN an old connection's Armed Status or Echo notification arrives after reconnect
  • THEN it cannot arm, satisfy current Echo or change current Status

BLE loss and recovery

BLE SHALL check matched Echo every 250 ms with a 500 ms deadline. Disconnect, GATT timeout or missing Echo SHALL clear intent, attempt bounded cleanup, alert once per outage and retry after one second. Initial and recovered connections SHALL require a fresh matching Echo before accepting R. Recovery SHALL discard outage input, start disarmed and require a new R and subsequent direction. Quit SHALL work during discovery, setup and retry.

Link returns with old keys pending
  • WHEN BLE reconnects after R/motion were typed during loss
  • THEN it reports reconnected disarmed only after matching Echo
  • AND it stays zero until fresh R and direction; failed retries do not repeat the loss beep

BLE ownership and shutdown

BLE connection SHALL be treated as the ownership claim and its lifetime as identity, without invented UDP session/release acknowledgements. Only the latest intent and a single pending control action SHALL be retained. Cleanup SHALL attempt zero, STOP/readback and disconnect within 500 ms total, even when earlier operations fail. Successful disconnect SHALL be reported separately from physical stop. The client SHALL not manage Wi-Fi policy or switch transports automatically.

Write fails during cleanup
  • WHEN zero or STOP fails or times out
  • THEN disconnect and terminal restoration are still attempted within their bounds
  • AND missing confirmation is reported honestly

openspec/specs/motor-control/spec.md

motor control

motor-control Specification

Purpose

Controls four motor channels independently with explicit enable, standby, duty mapping and fault behavior, without depending on device kinematics or transports.

Requirements

Four independent wheel commands

Motor control SHALL accept four signed wheel commands in −1.0..=1.0, ordered FL, FR, RR, RL. Positive means forward for that wheel. Magnitude SHALL be converted by the documented deadband/duty rule, not assumed proportional to physical speed. Each command SHALL affect its own wheel only, with no kinematic mixing.

Each wheel is driven on its own
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (0.5, 0, 0, 0)
  • THEN only FL is driven forward at the duty produced by the deadband/duty rule
  • AND FR, RR and RL receive a zero wheel command
Sign sets direction
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (−0.5, −0.5, −0.5, −0.5)
  • THEN every wheel turns in the direction that moves the car backward

Independent of transport and kinematics

Motor control SHALL expose configuration, wheel commands, enable/standby and typed validation faults. It SHALL NOT depend on setpoints, mecanum kinematics, the source or the session.

Built without the device layer
  • GIVEN the motor control module
  • WHEN it is compiled and host-tested on its own
  • THEN it builds without the setpoint, kinematics, arbiter or transport modules

Invalid wheel commands stop the wheels

Motor control SHALL clamp a finite wheel command outside −1.0..=1.0 to the nearest bound. A non-finite wheel command (NaN or infinity) SHALL put every driver in standby and report a fault, even when the other three are valid.

Out-of-range value is clamped
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (1.5, 0, 0, 0)
  • THEN FL is driven as for 1.0
NaN stops every wheel
  • GIVEN motor control is enabled and all four wheels are driven
  • WHEN it receives wheel commands (NaN, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
  • THEN every driver is put in standby
  • AND a fault is reported

Standby until explicitly enabled

Every motor driver SHALL be in standby from power-up, through reset and firmware recovery, until motor control is explicitly enabled. Disabling motor control SHALL put every driver in standby.

Boot does not move a wheel
  • GIVEN the car is powered off with motors connected
  • WHEN it powers up, resets, or recovers from a reset
  • THEN every driver's STBY input stays inactive until motor control is enabled
  • AND no wheel turns

Standby on safety stop

When the device raises a safety stop, the coordinator SHALL request standby in the control tick that processes the stop, and motor control SHALL set every wheel command to zero and deassert both STBY outputs before any further bridge update. A measured pin-level bound is deferred (O4: needs a logic analyzer or oscilloscope); this change SHALL NOT claim one.

Watchdog timeout puts every driver in standby
  • GIVEN the car is armed and all four wheels are driven
  • WHEN a watchdog timeout raises a safety stop
  • THEN both STBY outputs are deasserted in that control tick, before any further bridge update
  • AND on the bench every wheel stops

Full-scale maps to the configured limit

Wheel command 1.0 SHALL map to the configured maximum PWM duty, enforced independently for each wheel. The car SHALL use open-loop duty control without encoder feedback. The product profile SHALL cap drive duty at 70%, the envelope M4 verified (O1). Raising the cap SHALL require new qualification. Duty limiting SHALL NOT be advertised as current protection; start and stall current are not measured.

Product profile full scale
  • GIVEN the product profile: deadband 0.02, minimum duty 40%, maximum duty 70%
  • WHEN a wheel receives 1.0, then 0.5, then 1.5
  • THEN the requested duties are 70%, 55% and 70%
  • AND no command drives any wheel above 70%

Zero command behaviour

A zero wheel command SHALL request coast for that wheel without disabling a driven neighbour on the same driver. On the TB6612, this SHALL use IN1=IN2=low and PWM=high while STBY is high. A safety stop SHALL instead deassert both drivers' STBY inputs. Coast distance is not measured or claimed (O5). Source: Toshiba H-SW table, page 4.

Zero coasts a turning wheel
  • GIVEN a wheel driven at 0.5
  • WHEN it receives a zero wheel command
  • THEN its outputs are high impedance and it is allowed to coast
A zero wheel does not disable its neighbour
  • GIVEN FL and RL share driver 1 and motor control is enabled
  • WHEN FL receives zero and RL receives 0.5
  • THEN FL requests coast with both direction pins low and PWM high
  • AND RL retains its requested duty and driver 1 remains enabled

Dead zone handling

Exact zero or a magnitude below the configured deadband SHALL request coast. Otherwise duty SHALL be min + abs(command) * (max - min), rounded to permille after input clamping. The initial deadband SHALL be 0.02 and minimum duty 40%; maximum duty SHALL be configured. A precision minimum physical speed SHALL NOT be inferred from this rule. The stand starting observation was about 35%, not a universal per-wheel threshold.

Small command behaviour is predictable
  • GIVEN deadband 0.02, minimum duty 40% and maximum duty 100%
  • WHEN the wheel receives 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.5 and 1.0 in turn
  • THEN the requested modes/duties are coast, coast, 41.2%, 70% and 100%
  • AND negative commands use the same duty magnitude with reversed direction

Starts and reversals do not reset the controller

Motor control SHALL support direct signed changes, without a slew limit, up to the product cap. M4 reversed all four wheels between ±70% ten times without an ESP32 reset or BLE loss (O7). Operation above 70% SHALL NOT be claimed without new qualification.

Full reversal on all wheels
  • GIVEN the product profile (maximum 70%) and all four wheels at 1.0
  • WHEN all four are commanded to −1.0 in one control tick
  • THEN the ESP32-S3 does not reset and the owner's session survives

Calibrated wheel mapping

Motor control SHALL configure each wheel's driver channel and inversion. The current car mapping SHALL be D1 A→FL, D1 B→RL, D2 A→FR, D2 B→RR, with all inversions false because directions were corrected at connectors. Both separate STBY outputs SHALL follow motor enable/disable together.

Positive command moves each wheel forward
  • GIVEN the car restrained with wheels clear
  • WHEN each wheel in turn receives 0.3 alone
  • THEN the wheel at that position turns, in the direction that moves the car forward

Configuration validation

Before enabling, motor control SHALL validate finite deadband in [0,1), integer duty limits 0 ≤ min ≤ max ≤ 1000 permille, and a one-to-one mapping of four wheels to four bridge channels. Invalid configuration SHALL report a configuration fault and keep both drivers disabled. Configuration SHALL be immutable while enabled; replacing it SHALL disable and clear stored commands before validation.

Invalid duty or mapping cannot enable
  • GIVEN minimum duty 800 and maximum 700, or two wheels assigned to the same channel
  • WHEN configuration is installed and enable requested
  • THEN configuration is rejected and both STBY signals stay low
Invalid floating-point configuration cannot drive
  • GIVEN deadband NaN, infinity, negative or at least 1
  • WHEN configuration is installed
  • THEN a configuration fault is reported before any driver enable

Fault recovery requires explicit enable

A non-finite wheel vector SHALL invalidate stored commands and latch motor control disabled. Subsequent wheel updates SHALL NOT clear the latch. Explicit enable with a valid configuration and a complete finite wheel vector SHALL be required to recover; enabling SHALL NOT replay a previously stored vector. Standby SHALL always work, including in a fault state.

Valid updates do not clear a fault
  • GIVEN a NaN command caused both drivers to enter standby
  • WHEN several finite wheel updates arrive without explicit enable
  • THEN both drivers remain disabled
  • AND a later explicit enable with a new finite vector clears the command fault and applies only that vector

Complete vector validation before output

Motor control SHALL validate the entire vector before applying any channel, so a bad fourth value cannot partially drive the first three. Standby SHALL deassert both STBY outputs before preparing any new direction/PWM state. On enable, valid bridge states SHALL be prepared while disabled before STBY is asserted. Driver faults SHALL be reported to the caller, not silently converted to successful commands.

Fourth invalid wheel cannot cause partial motion
  • GIVEN drivers are disabled and a recording host driver
  • WHEN enable receives (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, infinity)
  • THEN no enable-high or drive update is issued for any bridge
Safe enable ordering
  • GIVEN disabled motor control with a valid configuration
  • WHEN it is explicitly enabled with a finite vector
  • THEN both drivers remain disabled until all four bridge states are prepared

Coast is independent of the drive duty cap

The configured maximum SHALL limit driven PWM duty, not the PWM-high signal required by the documented coast mode. A coast request SHALL keep both direction inputs low while PWM is high; it SHALL NOT become forward drive or brake merely because the configured drive cap is below 100%.

Coast with a reduced maximum
  • GIVEN maximum drive duty 70%, FL at zero and RL at 1.0
  • WHEN their shared driver is enabled
  • THEN FL has both direction pins low and PWM high, while RL is driven at 70%

openspec/changes/add-home-network-mode/design.md

Design

Context

See proposal.md for why. Today firmware/src/fw.rs builds one embassy-net stack on the AP interface with a static 192.168.4.1/24, and a wifi_gate task switches the AP off while BLE owns the car. rovi-core's Device::radio_allowed stops BLE advertising while a Wi-Fi source owns the car; wifi_allowed turns Wi-Fi off while BLE owns it. The ROS router endpoint is compile-time (ROVI_ZENOH_ROUTER, default tcp/192.168.4.2:7447, ADR-0012). esp-radio is built with coex; concurrent BLE and Wi-Fi traffic has not been characterized since M3 because ADR-0004 made it rare.

Todor's constraint: extend the current protocols and implementation minimally so existing tests and board evidence keep holding. Fallback mode must be byte-for-byte today's behaviour.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goals: the boot/override state machine in the specs; one network stack per mode; a per-mode ROS endpoint; BLE preemption only in home mode; host tests for every transition before any board run.

Non-Goals: AP+STA; changes to setpoint, Status, Echo, lease or claim-window rules; BLE preemption in fallback; ROS router discovery; WPA3; retry from fallback without reboot.

Decisions

D1. A network supervisor owns the mode (decided by Todor: protocol steps 1–3)

A firmware task runs attempt home → serve → (BLE override | link loss) → attempt home → … | fallback (terminal until reboot). The pure transition logic lives in rovi-core (testable on the host and in the simulator); the firmware task executes scan/join/DHCP/router steps with the budgets and reports outcomes to it. Alternative considered: deciding inside wifi_gate — rejected, it would mix radio switching with mode policy and is not host-testable.

D2. Station and AP are exclusive; one network stack per boot (builder's call, 2026-10-23)

A boot uses either the station interface with DHCPv4 (home attempt) or the AP interface with the static 192.168.4.1/24 (fallback), and the existing UDP and ROS tasks run unchanged on that one stack. Switching between them is a software reset with a one-word flag in persistent RTC memory: SWITCH | reason boots into fallback with that reason; power-on and every other reset attempt home. A BLE takeover in home mode does not reset: the station disconnects and later rejoins through a normal attempt. Considered: two live stacks (both interfaces exist in esp-radio 1.0.0-beta.1) with the UDP task on two sockets and the ROS adapter switching link managers — rejected for now: a second router link costs about 16 KB of RAM and would change the M8-validated UDP/ROS code paths, while mode switches are rare (a mode command, a failed attempt, a lost home network). Costs: an ev=boot reset=Sw line, a BLE watcher is dropped, and the reboot counts against the 2500 ms "AP up" budget, which board check 6.1 measures. AP+STA stays rejected by Todor.

D3. Preemption is one arbiter rule: BLE > UDP > ROS

Device gains a mode (Home/Fallback/Attempting). A claim from a higher-priority source preempts a lower one: UDP over ROS in both modes (same radio, no radio change); BLE over UDP/ROS in home mode only (in fallback BLE is not advertising while Wi-Fi owns, as today). The old owner gets StopReason::OwnerLost and is released; the new owner starts disarmed. No new stop reason or Status code. Alternative: a new Preempted reason, rejected because it changes Status on all three transports; the log shows it.

D4. Hand-back latch (decided by Todor: safe-by-default hand-back)

Preempting a ROS owner sets a latch in Device. When the preempting owner is released with Home pending, the latch clears and ROS auto-arms as today; otherwise the latch stays and the next ROS owner is claimed disarmed until it publishes /rovi/arm true (the existing STOP-latch path). This reverses the earlier "any BLE drop hands back immediately" for accidental drops only.

D5. Home settings are build variables (decided by Todor: option 3)

ROVI_HOME_SSID, ROVI_HOME_PASSWORD and ROVI_HOME_ROUTER are read with option_env! like ROVI_WIFI_PASSWORD; a const check (or build.rs) fails the build when the set is partial or invalid. The fallback-mode router endpoint stays ROVI_ZENOH_ROUTER / tcp/192.168.4.2:7447. Changing networks means rebuilding and flashing over USB. Todor's home settings live in gopass entry env/rovi/home (ROVI_HOME_SSID, ROVI_HOME_PASSWORD, ROVI_HOME_ROUTER); load them per shell with secenv env/rovi/home before building. Alternatives rejected: BLE provisioning (passphrase over unencrypted BLE, ADR-0008), BLE with pairing (more work on car and clients), a USB serial settings command with flash storage (new storage and protocol for a rare operation).

D6. Mode command and network information on every transport

Same rule everywhere (owner, disarmed, pending until release), parsed in rovi-core:

Mode command Network information
BLE Control codes 3 (Home), 4 (Car network) New Network characteristic d47a0016-…, read + notify
UDP Kind 10, payload 1/2, reply STATUS Kind 11, any peer, like Echo
ROS /rovi/mode std_msgs/UInt8 from the owner node /rovi/network std_msgs/String logfmt, ≥1 Hz and on change

Network information is mode=… pending=… fallback=… ip=… (BLE/UDP: a fixed 8-byte binary form: mode, pending, reason, reserved, IPv4). UDP is available in home mode with no extra code because the UDP task binds to whichever stack is active; trust is the home network (ADR-0008 superseded for station mode).

D7. Budgets

Scan ≤1500 ms (spec); join + DHCP + router ≤8000 ms after the network is found (raised from 5000 ms by Todor on 2026-10-26 after board check 6.1 measured 4.5 s on good runs and a 2 s router retry; ADR-0016's "~5 s" predates this). Every home-mode attempt (boot, after a BLE disconnect, after station loss) uses the same budgets, starting when the attempt starts. Builds without the ros feature ignore home settings and always fall back (home mode requires a ROS router). The scan step tries up to three times inside its budget (one active scan takes ~160 ms and missed the network about 1 in 30 boots on the board; a missing network still falls back in ~1.8 s). Values are compile-time constants, logged per step so they can be tuned from board data. The router step reuses the existing zenoh session open with a deadline instead of its retry loop.

D15. The router host is blackbox, on its cable (decided by Todor, verified 2026-10-28)

The home ROS router is rmw_zenohd from ROS 2 Jazzy (rmw_zenoh_cpp 0.2.11, the version CI and the bench use) in a Docker container, run by a systemd unit in ~/mycfg (hosts/blackbox/modules/rovi-ros-router.nix). Blackbox is always on; blade is a laptop and hosts nothing permanent. Facts that shaped it:

  • The car uses tcp/blackbox.local:7447; firmware resolves it to IPv4 before passing a literal endpoint to zenoh-nostd. Every connection attempt performs a fresh lookup. No DHCP reservation is needed (the devolo is a bridge; the gateway supplies DHCP).
  • TCP 7447 must be open on every interface that can carry the LAN (the first version opened Wi-Fi only; the car would have been refused).
  • A host with two interfaces on the home subnet must set arp_ignore=1/arp_announce=2: otherwise it answers the car's ARP request on both, the car may cache the Wi-Fi MAC, and its traffic is lost on the unusable Wi-Fi path (the car stalled right after its first batch; found on the board 2026-10-28). Applied in ~/mycfg.
  • The kernel sysctls showed loose filtering (rp_filter=2), not strict filtering as initially reported. The ARP captures and successful before/after fix establish ARP flux; they do not identify the exact packet-drop mechanism.
  • Blackbox on Wi-Fi alone was unusable for transfers (200-1500 ms latency, broken SSH streams): the router host must be cabled.

D14. BLE is quiet while a home attempt runs (board-measured, 2026-10-26)

With both BLE slots advertising, the Wi-Fi scan took 2.7 s instead of 160 ms (coexistence), past the scan budget. Device::radio_allowed(Ble) is false while attempting; BLE advertises again in home mode or fallback. The attempt lasts at most about 9.5 s (1.5 s scan, 8 s join budget), during which the car cannot be driven anyway.

D10. BLE claims on the first command; two connection slots

HostResources grows to two connections. A connection is unclaimed until its first Setpoint or Control write, which calls the existing claim path (so preemption, BUSY and the claim window apply then). Reads, notifications and Echo never claim. Losing ownership still disconnects that central (D8); the other stays. Existing clients write ARM or a setpoint right after connecting, so they claim as before. Alternative: one slot with an idle timeout, rejected because a watcher would block the rescue controller.

D11. One UDP observer query

UDP kind 11 INFO is answered to any peer, like Echo, with capabilities (the HELLO_ACK payload), Status and network information in one datagram. One query instead of three keeps the UDP surface small and lets a watcher poll everything it needs.

D12. ROS release and takeover notice

/rovi/release (std_msgs/Empty, owner node only) calls the same release path as UDP BYE. On preemption the arbiter emits a final Status for the old owner before switching: firmware sends it as a UDP STATUS to the old endpoint or publishes /rovi/status; BLE, the highest rank, is never preempted.

D13. One conformance suite for all transports

The shared rules (claim, arm, stop, lease, preemption, mode command, hand-back, observation, release, errors) are written once as transport-independent scenarios and run against the simulator through three adapters: UDP, ROS and a BLE GATT adapter. New rules are added once and proven on all three. Board acceptance stays separate (ADR-0002).

Risks / Trade-offs

  • [Two BLE connections plus Wi-Fi traffic raise coexistence load and RAM use] → measured in 6.3; watchers are read-only and notifications are small.

  • [Clients that relied on "connect = claim" to see claimed at once] → the laptop and iPhone clients write first; their tests are rerun (task 5.1).

  • [BLE advertising while ROS streams over Wi-Fi adds coexistence jitter] → board check of ROS round trip and Echo loss with advertising on, compared with the 2026-10-20 ROS soak baseline.

  • [A manual takeover ends by accident while ROS still streams] → hand-back latch (D4): ROS needs /rovi/arm true. Stock tools without an arm publisher cannot resume after an accidental drop; a deliberate Home hand-back keeps them working.

  • [Any home-network UDP client can take the car from a ROS controller] → accepted: the home network is trusted, and the preempted car stops disarmed.

  • [Anyone in BLE range can preempt the car in home mode] → unchanged ADR-0008 BLE risk; the home passphrase never goes over the air.

  • [Runtime stack switch unsupported by the beta radio driver] → D2's reset fallback.

  • [DHCP address of the router host changes] → the endpoint is built in by IP; give the router host a DHCP reservation or rebuild. Discovery is out of scope.

  • [Passphrase in the firmware image] → the image is local and flashed over USB; it is not published. Like ROVI_WIFI_PASSWORD, the variables come from the shell environment (e.g. gopass), never from a committed file such as the tracked .envrc.

Migration Plan

Without home settings the build behaves exactly as today, so existing images, clients and bench procedures need no change. Rollback is reflashing the previous image.

D8. BLE release ends the connection

As today (fw.rs disconnects a BLE central that lost ownership), a BLE owner released by its claim or reclaim window is disconnected; in home mode that disconnect starts a home-mode attempt unless Car network is pending. So Wi-Fi never comes back while a BLE central stays connected.

D9. Leaving fallback

Fallback has no automatic retry (it would blink the AP off every scan). A Home command from any owner, applied at release, is the only way back without a reboot.

Open Questions

  • Whether the ROS router step should also wait for the controller's liveliness tokens — settle from board data; does not change the specs.

D16. Resolve the configured router name before connecting (#115)

Todor requested name resolution on 2026-10-28. Enable embassy-net dns/mdns; its DNS socket already fits StackResources<6>. Resolve A records on every connection attempt, bounded at 3 seconds and still cancelled by the existing home-attempt deadline. Normalize case because smoltcp 0.12 selects mDNS with a lowercase suffix comparison. .local uses legacy unicast-response mDNS queries from an ephemeral port: no multicast listener/group join is needed. Other names use DHCP DNS. Numeric IPv4 endpoints bypass the lookup. Failed lookups retry until the home budget ends, then fallback; no stored-IP fallback or zenoh patch.

Log resolve with result, duration and IPv4 (zero on failure). Board evidence is in router-by-name notes. Router restart also exposed a 90-second Docker stop wait; the blackbox unit now explicitly stops its container (docker stop -t 5, TimeoutStopSec=20). Fresh-name lookup on reconnect is verified; an actual DHCP address change and cable-unplugged operation are not qualified.

openspec/changes/add-iphone-network-controls/design.md

Design

Use the existing Network characteristic (d47a0016-45b2-4d19-8db0-6bd87e9c0001), BLE Control 3 (Home) and 4 (Car network). Keep the four required characteristics unchanged; Network is optional for older firmware. Read its initial value and subscribe to notifications when supported; read it again to confirm a pending command.

Decode the existing eight-byte layout strictly: mode, pending, fallback reason, reserved zero and four IPv4 octets. Unsupported/malformed network information disables network controls, without granting or revoking motion permission. The core Status checks remain authoritative for control safety.

Extend the existing single-operation session procedure with a network command. Reject invalid targets or armed/busy sessions locally. Submit zero, write the mode command with response, read fresh Status, then read fresh Network and require the matching pending request. Zero setpoints between GATT round trips retain the existing 200 ms stream guard without relaxing the control deadline. A refused command remains connected/disarmed; a failed or unconfirmed operation closes through existing cleanup. Successful confirmation also uses existing cleanup/disconnect, preserving pending mode through STOP. Never send ARM.

The network panel uses explicit action buttons rather than a persistent toggle: the mode applies only after Bluetooth ownership ends, and Home is also the deliberate hand-back command when already in home mode. Show last-reported information after disconnect, with a reconnect-to-check message. An all-zero home address is unavailable; it is normal while BLE owns the car and Wi-Fi is paused. Do not expose SSID/password fields.

Tests exercise decoding, optional/legacy characteristic discovery, notifications and listener cleanup, both command paths, refusal, stalled work, generation changes and armed guards. Chromium tests cover the rendered controls and absence of ARM/nonzero commands. Physical phone validation is a separate acceptance task; this change does not close the deferred range test in home mode.

Firmware rejects the acknowledged ATT write on refusal. The client reads fresh Status after either write outcome; only an acknowledged write plus error-free disarmed Status and matching pending Network can confirm success. A reported refusal stays connected; an unexplained failed write closes as unconfirmed.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/design.md

M6 implementation design

Context

See proposal for scope and evidence. M8 has a host-tested no_std core plus separate firmware and simulator packages; M4 added a pure motor mapping function that currently imports the arbiter state. The working firmware remains our bench reference. This change extracts that behavior and applies the reviewed corrections, with no automatic flash or measurement sweep.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goal: independent motor control, one device contract for all transports, explicit validation/fault boundaries and repeatable conformance tests. Non-goals: a new HAL framework, closed-loop velocity control, runtime tuning UI or new physical qualification claims. The current geometry and accepted M5 references remain the inputs; no gain fitting is planned.

Decisions

Package boundaries

Cargo.toml                      workspace: reusable no_std crates only
crates/rovi-core/                codecs, arbiter, geometry, graph, device
crates/rovi-motor-control/       configuration, mapping, enable/fault state
crates/rovi-drive/               coordinator: device state → motor control, fault → device stop
apps/simcar/                    separate workspace/lockfile; host adapters
firmware/                      separate workspace/lockfile; ESP32 adapters
experiments/                   retained standalone bench reference

Exclude apps/simcar, firmware and the existing experimental packages from the root workspace. M8 separated host ROS dependencies and ESP dependencies because their crypto dependency resolutions conflicted; M6 will preserve that separation rather than solve unrelated dependency upgrades. Product applications depend on the reusable crates by path. Keep the pinned zenoh fork and current target/toolchain settings initially.

Copy the working core and tests into the product crates, preserving source history through the extraction commit. Experiments stay independently buildable and frozen as evidence; subsequent product fixes live in the product crates. This bounded duplication preserves rollback and avoids silently changing the firmware used to obtain old results. After product acceptance, archive the experiments as references rather than maintaining two active implementations.

rovi-core returns normalized wheel demands and state effects. It does not import the motor driver or HAL. rovi-motor-control has no dependency on the arbiter, kinematics or transports. The coordinator, rovi-drive (2026-10-17), connects them; it depends on both, so the integration and fault-injection tests run on the laptop, which a coordinator inside the ESP32-only firmware would not allow. A small output boundary (rovi_motor_control::Driver: STBY per driver, pins per bridge) exposes standby and bridge updates to the ESP implementation or a recording test double; no generic robotics framework is needed. All three crates build without std.

Drive::new(motor, &mut Device) binds before transport startup. Invalid motor configuration inhibits explicit ARM with not-ready and prevents ROS auto-arm before the first tick; the core only sees readiness, with no dependency on the motor crate. The firmware logs invalid boot motor configuration as motor_config. The simulator defaults to ready without a physical driver.

Drive::tick(&mut Device, now) runs every control tick: the device's timers first, then the motors. A change of the arbiter's arm_count is the only enable operation, so a STOP and re-ARM between two ticks still drops STBY first; while armed it updates the bridges, otherwise it puts both drivers in standby. It returns the device Effects and the tick's motor fault as an events::Fault (ev=error src=motor_*); Drive::motor().fault() gives the typed detail.

Configuration and fault boundary

Validate immutable device and motor profiles before accepting control. Canonicalize advertised floating values through f32 and use those values for limit comparisons, so a limit read over BLE is actually accepted. Geometry normalization remains 40 rad/s and reference limits 1/1/3 in the named experimental profile, not measured physical maxima. The product motor profile is minimum duty 40%, deadband 0.02 and maximum 70% (O1); the experiment firmware keeps its 100% cap as the comparison reference. No profile is labelled production-qualified merely because it compiles.

Motor operations are explicit enable with a complete vector, update while enabled, and standby. Validate the full vector before any drive output. A bad vector disables and latches the motor layer; ordinary updates cannot clear it. Prepare all bridge states while standby is inactive before enabling. Preserve 20 kHz PWM and the separate standby pins. Coast uses the datasheet pin state even when the drive duty cap is less than 100%.

On a motor validation failure, the coordinator immediately requests device out-of-limits stop, records the typed internal fault, and keeps both drivers disabled. This reuses existing status codes rather than introducing an incompatible reason enum. Only a fresh accepted setpoint followed by explicit ARM can call motor enable again; checking state == Armed on every tick is not an enable operation. Invalid motor configuration cannot be recovered through remote ARM; replace the configuration while disabled or reboot with a valid build. Invalid device configuration fails control initialization entirely.

Input processing and ownership

Process due deadlines before input; then validate envelope/identity, payload, ordering and limits before committing state. An initial ROS claim requires a known publisher and a finite, planar, supported-frame, in-limits setpoint. Out-of-limits input from an existing owner raises a stop; malformed, stale or non-owner input does not mutate the lease or sequence history.

Use wrapping u32 ordering for BLE/UDP. ROS keeps full i64 counters per publisher GID, including separate arm and setpoint streams; compare only within the same stream, then order valid samples from different owner publishers by receipt. Keep bounded graph identity and session ordering tables (16 entries each initially). Graph removal invalidates identity, but retain all accepted owner GID high-water marks until session release; unrelated graph churn cannot reset replay checks. Drop input from additional owner publishers if no ordering slot remains. Unknown publishers cannot drive until announced again. A live publisher must not reset its sequence under an unchanged GID; it must create a new publisher. ROS sequence values are not narrowed to u32.

UDP session allocation uses a boot-randomized nonzero u32 seed and increments per new claim, skipping zero; a current owner's repeated HELLO is idempotent. BLE callbacks carry a local connection generation to distinguish reused handles. Clear queued inputs on release and adapter reconnect. ROS has no Rovi session ID in its payload: these measures isolate local queues and known publisher lifetimes, but do not promise authenticated replay prevention across router/client restarts. Security remains the trusted local-link baseline in ADR-0008.

BLE disconnect and UDP BYE release their owning session. A detected ROS router disconnect does the same; publisher silence or missing liveliness triggers the independent lease path when fresh setpoints cease. Reconnect rebuilds graph state and declarations before samples can claim again. Wi-Fi stays up for both UDP and ROS; the arbiter performs their mutual exclusion.

ROS capabilities and status

Use shared typed capabilities/status snapshots; adapters serialize the same values. Preserve existing BLE/UDP frame layouts and numeric status codes. Implement persistent last-control-error state for every transport, not only BLE. BLE refreshes its readable value synchronously with changes; UDP sends its existing STATUS frame on owner control replies and stop transitions. Release leaves the externally readable state open; owner-lost is also recorded as a stop event, not a persistent stopped state with no owner.

ROS uses bounded CDR strings and the exact key/units contract in the spec. Both ROS adapters compare the shared Status snapshot every 10 ms and publish observed changes plus a 900 ms heartbeat; reconnect resets the publication schedule. session=0 denotes no owner. BLE refreshes the GATT value before reads and after control/setpoint writes, then notifies changes. UDP adapters poll for pending owner stop notifications even without incoming datagrams; unsolicited STATUS uses sequence 0, direct replies echo the request sequence. No measured velocity field is added.

O9 closed on 2026-10-17: the pinned ordinary publisher did not serve retained history to a late Jazzy transient-local subscriber; the same subscriber received its later live sample (evidence). Use the approved reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback. capabilities::Publication publishes every 900 ms (headroom under one second) and on observed session/owner changes; each new router connection starts a fresh schedule. Both adapters poll it every 10 ms and serialize Device::capabilities_snapshot() through the same bounded CDR encoder. Controllers subscribe with volatile durability. Transport disconnection can delay delivery; publication schedules are not guarantees during packet loss or an unavailable router.

Compatibility changes to verify

Compared with M8, intentionally correct per-wheel coast, validate configuration, latch internal motor faults, support u32 rollover and full ROS per-publisher ordering, reject unsupported frames, and process deadlines before commands. Preserve ROS auto-arm only for claim/lease-expiry and explicit ARM after STOP/out-of-limits. Add the already-agreed ROS capabilities/status content and consistent owner error persistence. These are contract improvements, not claims that extraction is behavior-identical. Client golden vectors retain version 1 layouts; existing client tools remain the bench interface.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Coast differs from the experiment's all-low output: reproduce the pin mismatch in a failing host test first; product physical stopping remains unqualified until bench acceptance.
  • Lower-layer fault accidentally re-enables on the next tick: integration tests inject faults through the coordinator and exercise continued ROS streaming, explicit recovery and session release.
  • Independent ROS publishers cannot share a sequence counter: per-GID histories plus same-node authorization; test duplicate, out-of-order and interleaved publishers.
  • Extraction breaks the target build or Python tools: keep separate app lockfiles, run existing socket/ROS scenarios against the product sim and cross-build both firmware features.
  • Known measurements are narrow: carry their evidence labels; do not replace normalization or claim electrical/stopping maxima from short pulses.

Migration and acceptance

Implement in the order in tasks: baseline extraction, motor seam, device conformance, ROS observability, then qualified firmware acceptance. Tests accompany each behavioral correction. Add product checks alongside existing experiment CI while the old firmware remains the rollback reference; update client/runbook executable paths when the product sim and firmware exist.

The scenario-to-test index is created before implementation and completed with actual test names/results as each task lands. Host-only scenarios stay host-only; radio, physical output, timing and thermal claims require their corresponding bench evidence. No motor run or flash is implicit in proposal acceptance.

Deferred qualification

O1, O2, O5 and O7 are decided (2026-10-17): 70% product cap, measured geometry with approximate references, coast for a zero wheel, direct reversals within the cap. This change does not claim what was not measured:

Not claimed Needs
Start and stall current (O1) A current monitor (INA226) or an oscilloscope with a shunt
Numeric STBY disable bound (O4) A logic analyzer or oscilloscope
Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband and coast with a driven neighbour (task 5.2, skipped by Todor 2026-10-19) A multimeter/logic probe for static levels; timing/PWM-capable tools for duty/deadband checks
Operation above 70% (O1, O7) Requalification with the equipment above
Coast distance and maximum speeds (O5, O2) Tape and video; not scheduled

They return as a new change when a requirement needs them. O9 is the laptop capability test with the fixed fallback above. No new measurement sweep is scheduled.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-laptop-teleoperation/design.md

Laptop teleoperation design

Context

See the proposal for motivation and accepted laptop scope. The existing car API and M6 evidence are the boundaries. apps/simcar/scenarios/wire.py already supplies golden-tested TwistStamped, Status and capability codecs; its scenario Client is a test helper, not a product transport.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goal: one small Linux terminal client whose policy can be tested with injected time and socket/terminal boundaries. Non-goals: a client framework, configurable bindings/speeds, multi-axis mixing, runtime firmware changes, station networking or proof of physical velocity/stopping distance.

Decisions

  • Use Python’s standard library (socket, select, terminal facilities, monotonic time), invoked from the repository as python3 -m apps.teleop --target HOST:PORT. No new runtime dependency or global installation. A browser UI or gamepad adds another input/runtime boundary without being needed for this first interface.
  • Keep policy separate from terminal/socket effects: a current intent, expiry, local arm gate and pending request deadlines. A single event loop handles input/replies before a 50 ms stream tick; no thread or command queue. Reject leases below 200 ms rather than promise a faster supported host cadence. A 200 ms scheduling gap fails closed; this is host policy, not a measured wheel-stop bound.
  • Use R for arm, WASD translation, QE rotation, Space STOP, Esc/Ctrl-C quit. Terminal bytes provide key repeats, not trustworthy key-up/focus events: each direction is a 250 ms request that needs renewal. Drain buffered input to the latest motion intent; stop/quit overrides that batch, and arming clears it. Never replay accumulated input after a scheduling gap. Zero intent keeps the owner’s lease live while idle/disarmed; Space sends STOP while retaining the session and zero stream.
  • Share, rather than copy, the existing payload codec in a small apps/client Python package. Keep a thin compatibility import at the existing scenario module path so bench/ROS/experimental users retain their imports and golden tests. Add frame validation in the client boundary; avoid converting every existing test helper into a production client in the same change.
  • Correlate every control reply by endpoint, session and a nonzero request sequence; preserve unsolicited sequence-zero stops separately. Use wrapping u32 setpoint ordering independently. Only one ARM may be pending. If a stopped notification arrives while ARM is pending, cancel that request locally; a delayed Armed reply cannot revive local motion. A later R sends zero and a new request. Do not retry ARM automatically.
  • Echo checks only reachability. UDP has no observational owner-status read, and HELLO can claim after a reset. Therefore perform HELLO only once and label Status as last reported with its own age. A reset may leave a responsive car rejecting the old session; this client never claims it silently. A new operator-started process is required to reclaim after terminal/link failure.
  • All connect/control waits and cleanup are bounded. On exit try zero, STOP, BYE; catch individual send failures so later cleanup still runs, then restore terminal state in an outer finally block. STOP success needs the matching state/reason acknowledgement; BYE has no release acknowledgement and remains best effort. No promise that the wheel stopped merely because a datagram was sent.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Terminal repeat may begin after the 250 ms window, producing an initial pause → document this pulse/renewal behavior; deterministic expiry matters more than pretending key-up exists.
  • Wi-Fi can silently stall (#23) → missed Echo deadlines end the client, the device lease remains independent, and no reconnect is automatic. This change does not diagnose or close #23.
  • UDP can lose a stop or release → bounded best effort and explicit unconfirmed reporting; retain the device watchdog. No application-level emergency-stop guarantee.
  • Existing source/net and motor bench evidence does not qualify a new terminal application → simulator/PTY evidence first, then a separately announced gentle stand batch; no loaded/floor test or electrical measurement is implied.

Migration and rollback

Add the client without firmware or API changes. Preserve the current codec import through a compatibility module and rerun its existing tests and simulator scenarios. Keep the normal ROS firmware installed. Rollback removes the new application and restores the codec location; no board image or protocol migration is needed.

Scope decision

Todor selected the laptop client on 2026-10-20 after reviewing the concrete option in #89. Implementation uses the proposed keys, 250 ms intent window and gentle defaults; no new ADR is needed for these reversible client choices.
