openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-21-add-iphone-ble-client/design.md

iPhone BLE web controller design (draft)

Context

See proposal for the selected scope and acceptance gate. The accepted car API remains unchanged. The laptop client supplies the gentle-direction/explicit-arm precedent; UDP handshake/correlation does not apply to BLE. Q9/Q18/Q19/Q21 remain the roadmap's home.

Recorded user decisions (2026-10-20)

  • Linux only; no Mac or paid Apple Developer membership; avoid a subscription.
  • Target a web controller opened in Bluefy on iPhone.
  • Phone supports the 72-byte payload (Todor's confirmation, not a new measured app/board result).
  • Six press-and-hold buttons first; allow a later accelerometer-based input without changing the device API or bypassing safety policy. Todor then explicitly accepted the revised proposal for button implementation; see acceptance record.

Existing protocol evidence

Inspected at main 1be50b3; no protocol change is proposed.

Concern Existing evidence and client consequence
Advertisement/claim Firmware BLE loop: flags and Rovi M8 in scan response, no service UUID. Use a name filter plus optional service access, then validate GATT. Connecting claims immediately and switches off the AP. Name/device ID is not authentication.
GATT RoviService: service d47a0010-45b2-4d19-8db0-6bd87e9c0001; same suffix with 0011 Setpoint (write without response), 0012 Control (write with response), 0013 Capabilities (read), 0014 Status (read/notify), 0015 Echo (write without response/notify). Require the first four characteristics/properties; Echo is unused.
Setpoint Python wire reference and Rust decoder: u32 LE sequence + 68-byte little-endian TwistStamped CDR = 72 bytes. Empty frame means base_link; zero timestamp is valid; only vx/vy/wz vary. No UDP header, BLE numeric session, HELLO or BYE.
Capabilities Encoder: u8 version, five f32 LE (radius, centre projection sum, max_vx/max_vy/max_wz), three u16 LE (lease/claim/reclaim ms), 27 bytes. Widen f32 values exactly; never round limits upward.
Status/control Encoder: states 0 Open/1 Claimed/2 Armed/3 Stopped; reasons 0 none/1 Stop/2 LeaseExpired/3 OwnerLost/4 OutOfLimits; errors 0 none/1 Busy/2 NotOwner/3 NotReady/4 Invalid. Require reason=0 except Stopped, whose reason must be nonzero. ARM=1/STOP=2; refused writes use ATT Value Not Allowed.
Windows Defaults: lease 1000, claim 10000, reclaim 5000 ms. Read advertised values. Disarmed zero setpoints retain ownership; STOP retains it; disconnect releases it. Firmware disconnects on ownership expiry.
Prior evidence Bleak client, product Status/Echo probe and BLE lease results inform the wire contract, not Bluefy performance.

Goals / Non-Goals

Goals: Linux-authorable static controller, one foreground phone session, button-first operation, testable codecs/session policy and separate browser/radio/wheel evidence.

Non-Goals: native app/scaffold/signing, sensor driving in v1, firmware/security changes, station mode, background driving, automatic recovery, calibration or measured speed. No hosted site is published by this change until task 3.2.

Decisions

Bluefy web delivery from Linux

Use static HTML/CSS/JavaScript under apps/iphone/ with no third-party runtime scripts. Load a versioned page over HTTPS in Bluefy. No command backend, account or paid developer membership is needed for our web code. Propose a repository GitHub Pages deployment at https://tptodorov.github.io/rovi/iphone/ (not a live URL claimed by this draft). GitHub Pages supports static sites in public repositories on GitHub Free. Prepare only the app assets, preserving any existing site configuration; confirm the final origin/HTTPS during delivery. The page is trusted controller code: no third-party runtime scripts or secrets. This spec PR performs no deployment.

Why this route: Apple's Xcode requirements require macOS; free Personal Team provisioning uses Xcode and expires after seven days. A remote Mac can compile a native app, but compilation alone does not solve free signing/install from this Linux setup. Bluefy's developer guide documents HTTPS-page BLE control; its App Store listing lists it as free. This replaces the earlier SwiftUI/CoreBluetooth proposal rather than adding a second client.

Bluefy is a required installed host, not proof that every Web Bluetooth function or inactive-state signal works on the selected phone. Feature checks and P1/P3 must fail closed where support is absent. Safari/Home Screen web apps are not promised substitutes; WebKit's tracking issue records the Web Bluetooth limitation. No Expo/React Native wrapper is needed.

Selection and setup

The page's Choose & Connect action explains the ownership/AP effect, then invokes requestDevice with filters: [{name: 'Rovi M8'}] and optionalServices: [serviceUUID]. Selecting in the browser picker is the explicit target choice; only then connect while the page is active. Picker presentation/dismissal is browser-controlled: do not promise a custom scan list, RSSI, hardware addresses, a cancellable scan API or a ten-second picker timeout. Same-name candidates are not authenticated identities; display the selected name and opaque browser ID when available.

Start the ten-second setup deadline at GATT connect invocation after selection, not while the person considers the picker. Discover/validate required properties, exact capabilities, valid Claimed/Stopped Status and notifications; submit an initial 72-byte zero setpoint without response, with no ARM. Claim starts before discovery completes; a firmware timeout fails setup without automatic reconnect. Reject lease<500 ms, claim<1000 ms or invalid/nonpositive windows/geometry. Current defaults exceed these supported-profile floors; these are proposed client bounds, not iOS measurements.

The phone payload capability is user-confirmed. Web Bluetooth does not expose CoreBluetooth's MTU/write-capacity/readiness APIs. Show packet size 72 and MTU/capacity as unavailable unless actually measured externally. A rejected initial zero submission is incompatibility; promise resolution is not proof of firmware receipt. An explicit later zero+ARM/Status transaction and P1 establish the browser/firmware path. Never fragment or switch protocols automatically.

Button input with a later sensor option

Separate the input interpreter from the session/transmitter: buttons produce only latest planar intent and its expiry; one shared policy owns arming, caps, STOP, lifecycle and connection generations. No generic plugin framework or unused sensor implementation is needed. A future accelerometer/tilt interpreter would feed that same intent boundary; it cannot arm or write GATT directly. It needs a separate reviewed proposal for axis mapping, calibration, dead zone, enable/deadman gesture, permission refusal, sensor loss and input switching. The motion/orientation standard defines sensor APIs, not a guarantee that Bluefy exposes them. V1 does not request motion permission or consume sensor data.

The v1 page has Choose & Connect, local/reported state, ARM, prominent STOP, six labelled hold buttons, requested values and Disconnect. Buttons use pointer tracking/capture with explicit bounds checks; pointerup/cancel, lost capture, leaving bounds or another direction invalidates the hold. Renew the held input only from active visible UI animation frames, never the transmit timer; a stalled UI expires after 250 ms even if BLE work continues. Re-entry requires a new press. Text/accessibility labels, large targets, text sizing and cues beyond color apply; accessibility activation never creates a sticky nonzero toggle. Actual hold accessibility/usability remains a P3 acceptance check.

Stream, controls and Status

One session generation and operation epoch own all asynchronous work. Serialize GATT procedures; keep at most one pending setpoint write promise and one coalesced latest intent, never a motion queue. Every 50 ms, check lifecycle, stops and input expiry before choosing a sample. Do not start another write while the prior procedure is pending. A scheduler/submission gap>=200 ms fails the run; do not catch up. A write-without-response promise is host progress, not an acknowledgement of applied motion. Fair scheduling must leave space for Status/control within these bounds; P2 measures the complete workload.

ARM invalidates touches, submits fresh zero, then performs one writeValueWithResponse ARM. Only its successful current-generation promise plus the subsequently requested readValue result Armed/none/none grants local motion permission; one second covers the whole action. Copy the returned bytes immediately. Notifications never grant arm. Unlike native delegate callbacks, Web Bluetooth provides an explicit read promise; there is no need to repeatedly disable notifications to identify read results. Ignore stale promise completions and never use cached characteristic.value to confirm controls.

STOP immediately invalidates pending local ARM and all holds, takes scheduling priority, and requires successful Control=2 write plus a subsequent read Stopped/Stop/none within one second. An in-flight GATT procedure cannot be assumed cancellable; keep intent zero, attempt STOP when possible, and disconnect on timeout. Confirmed STOP retains zero streaming/ownership; only a new explicit ARM and new press can resume. Notifications can revoke permission; repeated reports of the same stopped state while recovering do not create a new stop, but a new stop transition during ARM invalidates it.

Schedule an explicit Status read every 500 ms, at most one pending transaction; a control confirmation read also counts. A transaction lasting>=1000 ms, malformed result, GATT error, Open or unexpected Armed ends the run. Status notifications/reads do not renew the firmware lease. Treat disconnection events and observed service/permission loss as failure. Web APIs need not expose native powered-off/resetting/permission distinctions: use specific errors when known and honest unavailable/disconnected wording otherwise.

Lifecycle and bounded shutdown

During setup/connection, use page visibility, blur, pagehide/navigation and any verified Bluefy host inactivity signal to clear holds and end the session. Before GATT connection, a browser picker can itself change focus; that focus change cannot drive anything. Recheck page activity after selection and never connect from an inactive page or a cancelled attempt. Gate every send on the current active/visible state; foreground return, page reload or a remembered device grant cannot reconnect or re-arm automatically. Do not opt into Bluefy background peripheral access or prevent screen locking. Browser/native lifecycle events are not interchangeable: P3 must verify actual lock, app switch, browser UI and interruption behavior; if an undetected inactive state allows renewed nonzero submissions, this browser/version is unsupported for driving.

Disconnect/failure first clears intent and stops the normal stream. Under one 500 ms deadline while runnable, independently attempt zero and STOP where possible, then invoke local gatt.disconnect() even if a promise fails/hangs. Cancel generations and ignore late completions; a connect promise resolving after shutdown is disconnected again. A browser picker cannot be forcibly dismissed by an invented API; a late selection never connects after its local attempt was cancelled.

Suspension/termination may prevent any cleanup. Firmware lease/window handling remains the independent fallback; local disconnect or resolved writes do not establish physical link teardown, ownership release or wheel stop. Show requested, device-reported and unconfirmed states separately, retaining the original Status observation age.

Platform sources checked 2026-10-20

Web Bluetooth specification defines secure-context user selection, service access, characteristic properties, separate write modes, read promises and notification events. These are API contracts, not evidence that Bluefy implements every method. Bluefy's official site and guide document its GATT bridge and HTTPS requirement. The App Store release notes mention a host app-state hook; exact hook registration/semantics must be verified instead of guessed. Apple's foreground/background guide explains why suspension cannot be treated as a runnable cleanup opportunity.

Original acceptance gates

Item How to settle Blocks
I1 — browser/environment and delivery checks Record iPhone model/iOS/Bluefy version. Confirm split write methods, read/notify, name-only picker and lifecycle signals. Verify the proposed GitHub Pages origin/HTTPS during delivery, preserving existing site configuration; publication remains a future authorized task. Linux-only/no-membership, Bluefy and the proposed free hosting route are recorded choices. Deployment and phone acceptance; independent Linux codec/UI/session work can proceed after task 1.1.
I2 — browser payload integration, phone capability confirmed Todor confirms phone 72-byte support. P1 checks the actual Bluefy path with zero+explicit ARM/Status at zero; keep runtime rejection handling. Record measured ATT MTU only if instrumentation provides it; do not fabricate capacity from Web Bluetooth or mark new board evidence passed. Browser compatibility acceptance, not a repeated question about whether the phone supports 72 bytes.
I3 — Q19 full workload P2 measures 60 s at 20 Hz with Status reads and zero ARM/STOP: no lease expiry, >=200 ms submission gap or one-second control/read timeout. Record connection interval only if measured. Failure requires reviewed changes, not silently relaxed bounds. Phone acceptance and motor batch; BlueZ results do not pass it.
I4 — lifecycle/accessibility verification Button-first interaction is selected. P3 verifies actual touch, text/accessibility, blur/hidden/lock/interruption behavior and no background renewal of motion. Missing host signals must still produce expiry/lease fallback; persistent hidden motion fails support. UI/phone acceptance, not the selected button layout.

These proposal-stage gates are retained for traceability. Implementation and scoped phone/stand acceptance completed on 2026-10-21; tasks and verification record the evidence, P2 closure decision and untested limits. Unmeasured browser/hardware results remain unclaimed.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • Browser dependency and opaque picker/state APIs → feature gates and actual-phone checks; no native feature assumptions or guessed host hooks.
  • Browser scheduling/buffered writes and suspension → expiring UI intent, bounded application work and firmware lease fallback. Proposed software deadlines are not physical stopping bounds.
  • Public static controller code and same-name peers → controlled HTTPS origin, no remote runtime scripts, explicit selection and GATT validation; these do not add authenticated identity to the existing API.
  • Zero streaming deliberately retains ownership after STOP → visible ownership effect and Disconnect. Open-loop gentle references can overcome motor deadband; they are not measured physical speeds.

Migration Plan

After explicit acceptance, implement/test the static page from Linux, prepare a reviewable HTTPS deployment, and publish only within an authorized delivery task. Then run separately authorized phone checks and a separately announced supervised wheels-off-ground batch. Rollback is disconnecting/closing the page and withdrawing its deployment; no firmware migration. Archive after product acceptance, never after this planning PR alone.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-22-add-iphone-physical-control/design.md

Physical input in the existing iPhone client

Boundary

Keep one Session owner and one serialized BLE stream. A small Physical interpreter beside Hold supplies bounded intent; it never arms, connects or writes BLE. Keep button Hold behavior intact. All Session invalidation paths clear button holds and Physical running state; close also disables physical input and discards calibration.

Input and permissions

Default Buttons. Selecting Physical does not request permission or claim a car. Selecting Physical or an explicit Retry calls the optional DeviceOrientationEvent permission method directly from that gesture, then installs generation-guarded orientation callbacks. No compass, motion.interval, gyroscope integration or sensor fusion is needed. Missing/null/ non-finite/out-of-range angles fail closed. Track optional absolute-reference metadata; a change invalidates calibration rather than silently changing the frame.

Set neutral & ARM takes the latest fresh sample while locally disarmed with no pending control, then follows the existing zero/ARM/read sequence. No separate calibration tap is required; every explicit ARM captures neutral, never a sensor callback. Neutral must be screen-up, beta/gamma within ±30°. Current beta/gamma must remain within ±60°, and shortest heading offset within ±90°. These explicit software limits keep the selected Euler mapping away from inversion/singular postures; they are not measured sensor-accuracy limits. Screen orientation changes end Physical sessions. Do not silently recenter or rotate axes under running Physical control.

Mapping

Use shortest signed angle differences, including alpha wrap at 0/360. Map negative delta-beta to +vx, negative delta-gamma to +vy and positive delta-alpha to +wz. Each component has a symmetric 3° dead zone, linear scale to full value at 20°, then saturation: min(0.1 m/s, advertised translation maximum), or min(0.3 rad/s, advertised rotational maximum). Zero axes stay zero. All three components may combine in Physical mode. Buttons continue to select one axis. No filtering initially: the user confirmed this preview, with quiet excursions below 0.05° for 13.1 s. Longer drift and mixed-motion physical bounds remain unverified.

State and recovery

Mode changes clear both inputs and calibration, revoke local arm, supersede ARM with STOP while ready, and cancel setup/picker attempts. A fresh ARM and new post-arm input action are mandatory. A ready connection can remain open after confirmed STOP. Permission alone never arms. Connecting discards earlier calibration; ARM completion clears input but preserves valid calibration.

Physical mode uses explicit tap START/PAUSE after confirmed Set neutral & ARM. START requires all three shortest offsets within ±3° of neutral, fresh valid orientation and active foreground; an early/rejected START is never queued. START latches running input, independent of finger release. PAUSE and scroll clear running input to zero while retaining arm/neutral; no sample can restart it. STOP, mode changes, ARM completion, cleanup and reported safety stops also clear running state. Buttons retain their existing held-pointer interpreter.

Only UI frames renew the Physical running deadline (250 ms); only new sensor callbacks renew sample freshness (250 ms). Test expiry before replacing samples or renewing a deadline, so resumed execution cannot hide a missed deadline. Sensor/posture loss while running or foreground-renewal expiry revokes calibration and ends through cleanup. When paused, gaps or reading posture block START at zero but retain neutral and arm. Invalid values/reference changes still close armed or arming sessions. Lifecycle return requires manual enabling, connection, ARM and START. No silent recentering or automatic recovery is introduced.

Keep requested motion and the applicable ARM/START/PAUSE action with STOP in the persistent thumb dock; arm state and the latest reason remain in a sticky status area. Give running/paused text and the offending angle/value/limit on posture faults. Screen-up tilt limits stay ±60° absolute, heading offset ±90°; the interface change does not establish a cause for the reported z-axis interruption. Earlier held-pad UX/neutral results are evidence for that build, not acceptance of this new interaction.

Keep 50 ms attempted sends, 200 ms scheduler/submission failure, Status validation, STOP priority and 500 ms runnable cleanup unchanged. Phone measurements found a 60 ms median for a nominal 50 ms local consumer: record actual BLE gaps rather than claiming exact 20 Hz. Firmware lease remains an independent fallback.

Evidence and remaining gates

Pure input tests plus Session fake-GATT and real-page browser tests cover this state model; they do not establish phone/BLE or physical stopping. Phone acceptance must combine sensors and the full BLE workload, exercise all invalidations and extend quiet evidence to 60 s. A separate stand batch covers six signs, mixed axes, neutral/PAUSE, STOP, mode changes and interruptions. No floor test is included.

Controller screen redesign

Todor requested a production-quality interface for both modes using design skills. Apply the local UX Designer and Web Interface Guidelines skills within this existing client, with no framework, remote font, runtime asset or hosting change. Keep Session, Hold, Physical, wire values and motor limits as the control boundary.

Portrait wireframe (compact, 320–390 px):

rovi / controller       connection · Connect/Disconnect
[       Buttons       |       Physical       ]
Phone arm state · next action / inline fault reason
[ six held directions OR live tilt/neutral visual ]
Requested: forward · sideways · turn
[ Connection & diagnostics (closed) ]
[ ARM / START / PAUSE              ][ STOP ]  thumb dock

Use system typography, warm neutral surfaces, forest-green identity, amber for armed/paused and red for STOP/faults. Support a matching dark palette. Use SVG icons/phone input visualization with text equivalents, tabular numerical values, 44 px minimum targets and visible keyboard focus. Default and connected phone screens must show controls and requested motion without scrolling; larger text may scroll with safe bottom padding so focus stays above the dock. Keep actual fault messages visible. Show technical Status, stream counters and raw angles in collapsed native details; opening it pauses input. Never animate motion merely for decoration or imply measured wheel feedback.

Choosing Physical from a user-operated native radio prepares orientation sensors in that same gesture; it never connects or arms. Allow this while a mode-change STOP is pending because local motion is already revoked. Permission denial or missing readings expose Retry; the normal path needs no separate Enable button. Retain epoch/generation/foreground guards and actual blur/hidden cleanup, including if an iOS permission dialog interrupts an existing connection. Native permission and Web Bluetooth may still require manual recovery on the phone; no permission exception weakens safety or promises a production qualification we have not tested.

Render text only when it changes, so a stable status is not re-announced every frame. Keep sensor previews separate from requested velocities; paused previews never authorize motion. Test compact/light/dark/200% text states plus permission, mode, input cancellation, STOP, diagnostics and lifecycle paths. This redraw needs a new motor-power-off Bluefy usability check; earlier phone results are historical.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-22-add-laptop-ble-teleoperation/design.md

Design

Context

The UDP loop uses socket readiness and request-correlated frames. BLE instead claims at connect and exposes async GATT writes, readable Status and notifications. The existing bench BLE client establishes UUIDs, BlueZ MTU acquisition and codecs.

Decisions

  • Add a native async BLE loop beside UDP, sharing Policy, terminal input, codecs and audio. Avoid a local fake-UDP bridge or broad transport refactor: GATT has no UDP session/control sequence to correlate. UDP's tested loop stays intact.
  • Use the installed Bleak dependency lazily. Bound discovery to five seconds (four-second scan plus setup/teardown margin), reject ambiguous name discovery, and connect with a five-second bound. A MAC pins every retry; name discovery must find exactly one matching advertisement and then pin its address. Recovery cannot roam to another advertising car.
  • Validate service/characteristics/properties, capabilities and MTU/write capacity before motion. Require a matching Echo before enabling keys. Use the established BlueZ MTU acquisition hook, with advertised write capacity as fallback; fail closed if 72-byte writes cannot be established.
  • Keep only latest intent and one pending control action, never a motion queue. Serialize GATT operations with short deadlines. ARM writes zero first and requires a successful ATT write plus fresh Armed Status read. Notifications never authorize ARM. Space/safety stops invalidate pending ARM confirmation.
  • Tie callbacks and Echo nonces to a connection generation. Ignore closed-peer callbacks. Drop buffered keys at readiness/reconnect, preserving quit. A lost connection clears motion before cleanup, one loss alert and a one-second retry.
  • Best-effort zero, STOP/readback and disconnect share a 500 ms cleanup budget; failed writes cannot skip disconnect. ATT success/readback is not wheel feedback. Bleak cancellation and terminal restoration also cover discovery/setup/quit.

Risks and limits

BLE ownership turns off the car AP; no simultaneous UDP/BLE control or seamless transport switching. Another owner prevents advertising, so discovery keeps retrying without stealing ownership. Direct sound can be muted or unavailable. Host fake-GATT tests cannot establish radio, MTU negotiation or physical stopping acceptance; those remain a separately authorized stand check.

API references

Bleak client documents write-with-response versus queued writes, characteristic capacity and BlueZ's MTU reporting limitation. Scanner documents discovery with advertisement data. Local installed API is checked through the project's Nix shell; no dependency upgrade is required.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-22-add-teleop-reconnect/design.md

Design

Context

The current client intentionally raises a fatal error for any missed reply. A PTY/fake-peer reproduction drops Echo and produces the reported timeout/exit. This establishes client behavior, not the cause of radio delay or packet loss.

Decisions

  • Keep the existing per-attempt Session and input Policy. A small outer retry loop handles typed link failures (HELLO/control/Echo timeouts, BUSY and socket errors). Invalid capabilities, terminal loss, input flood and scheduler gaps remain fatal. This avoids treating a broken terminal as a recoverable network.
  • Clear Policy before cleanup/alert, send zero/STOP/BYE best effort, then wait one second with quit input serviced. New attempts use fresh Session/Policy instances and monotonically advanced control sequences so old ACKs cannot satisfy a new HELLO. Retry respects ownership; BUSY never authorizes motion.
  • Require a fresh matched Echo before exposing recovered controls. Discard buffered keys at recovery boundaries, preserving quit; directions and R typed during the outage cannot resume motion. A post-recovery R and direction are necessary. Keep one loss alert latched until Echo confirms recovery.
  • Generate a short PCM tone with the standard library and play through existing pw-play. Playback is bounded and happens only after motion is disabled. Missing/failed audio reports a warning and falls back to terminal BEL. Muted hardware cannot be detected; an audible check remains physical evidence.
  • Retry the selected UDP endpoint only. NetworkManager keeps responsibility for AP association; the application does not switch networks or reset firmware.

Risks / Trade-offs

  • One dropped Echo can still trigger recovery: the 500 ms safety policy is preserved, rather than masking a slow link by widening deadlines.
  • Lost cleanup can leave the old owner until its lease/reclaim window ends; retries wait through BUSY. Reclaiming does not bypass device ownership.
  • Automatic reconnection improves usability but does not prove Wi-Fi stability, wheel-stop latency or physical safety. Host tests and board evidence stay separate.

Migration

The same command starts the client; retries replace the previous terminal exit. Reverting the client commit restores fail-and-exit behavior. No device change.

Verification

Implementation authorized by Todor's “do it” on 2026-10-28. No motors or ARM are needed for this change's phone check.

Host evidence

  • cd apps/iphone && rtk npm test: 63 passing Node tests, including 13 network tests. The first implementation run reproduced unsupported Network/absent mode behavior before the feature was added.   • Built-page Playwright/Chromium: 43 passing checks, including six new network cases. Existing direction, STOP, physical-control, responsive-layout and cached-release checks remain green.
  • A firmware-path review found ATT writes are rejected on mode refusal. Updating the fake to reject reproduced a failure (client disconnected instead of explaining refusal). Fresh Status now distinguishes rejection from an unconfirmed transport failure; a failed write cannot confirm an already-pending mode.
  • Network checks cover strict eight-byte decoding, optional/legacy characteristics, notifications, malformed metadata, armed/busy/invalid guards, Home and Car network requests, fresh matching confirmation, refusal, stalled operations, old callbacks and zero-only writes. Browser tests verify displayed state, last-reported labels, action guards and refusal guidance.

The no-motion hardware soak requested alongside this feature has separate evidence. It exercised existing firmware, not this phone implementation.

Required phone check — pending

Use the published revision in Bluefy, with motor power off. Do not ARM.

  1. Connect, open Connection, network & diagnostics, and check mode/address/pending information.
  2. Tap Use car network. Check confirmation and automatic Bluetooth disconnect. Reconnect and check the reported Car network state.
  3. Tap Use Home Wi-Fi. Check confirmation and disconnect. Reconnect after the home attempt and inspect reported mode/pending/reason/address. BLE ownership pauses home Wi-Fi, so the address can be unavailable while connected.
  4. Disconnect normally. Record the published build, phone/browser, visible outcomes and serial mode events when available.

No real iPhone/Bluefy result is claimed yet. Keep task 3.2 open and do not archive this change until it passes. Physical range fallback belongs to the home-network change and remains explicitly deferred.

CI coverage (task 3.6)

Workflow, with experiments retained alongside product checks:

Job Product checks
OpenSpec Strict active/baseline/archive validation; generated reader coverage, links and freshness.
Host All three crates: format, 214 unit tests and clippy. Sim car: format, clippy/build with and without ROS; 14 real UDP socket scenarios. Product Python: 23 codec/log/latency tests; 40 bench-harness tests covering BLE safeguards, UDP simulator probes and ROS serial-evidence gates. These do not prove board outputs.
ROS All six scripts: ros-scenarios.sh, ros-router-gone.sh, ros-reconnect.sh, ros-refresh.sh, ros-stale-session.sh, ros-capabilities.sh (includes capabilities and status observers). Scripts run sequentially because three use the same host router port/container name. CI also runs the board runners for read-only delivery, ROS stop/recovery, router loss, shared UDP/ROS ownership and ROS device-clock lease timing on loopback ports 17449–17453. No hardware is involved.
Firmware Product and experiment: clippy/build for ESP32-S3, with and without ROS. Product no_std crates are linked into both firmware variants. Motor crate dependency inspection shows no dependencies.

The merged software through task 3.5 passed all four main checks. The audit added the three previously local-only ROS scripts and sim clippy without ROS. It also reproduced and fixed invalid motor configuration reporting a successful ARM before the coordinator tick: ARM now reports not-ready on every source, including before the first tick. No test-count or existence check alone proves scenario coverage; the rows describe the assertions reviewed.

The prepared UDP board probe reuses the product socket client. test_udp_probe_against_product_simulator runs all four stop/recovery scenarios on loopback; test_lost_cleanup_bye_cannot_report_released drops BYE and requires the probe to reject missing serial release. That regression failed first before adding the release assertion. These simulator checks alone do not count as physical acceptance. The subsequent authorized board batch passed protocol assertions and Todor confirmed all four wheel stops, pauses and recovery.

The prepared ROS read-only board batch reuses ros_capabilities.py and ros_status.py before/after a router restart. Loopback results: capabilities late receipt 0.551/0.620 s, Status 0.755/0.751 s, maximum observed period 0.909 s, ownership changes about 0.010 s; no arming. The subsequent authorized ROS board batch passed both probes before/after router restart: capabilities late receipt 0.574/0.667 s, Status 0.766/0.783 s, largest observed period 0.908 s, claim/release updates 0.011–0.031 s. The serial link rejoined in 2.083 s and never armed. Actual ESP32 capabilities/Status delivery passed; this read-only batch did not test motors.

The ROS motor batch prepares STOP, lease expiry and out-of-limits checks using one node's cmd_vel/arm publishers. Each stop/recovery requires fresh serial and canonical Status evidence. STOP/limits must inhibit fresh streaming until explicit ARM; ROS lease recovery auto-arms on resumed input as specified. The identical runner is exercised on loopback in CI; the subsequent authorized board batch passed every protocol/serial assertion. Todor confirmed all four wheel stops, pauses and explicit/automatic recoveries at vx=0.1 (“Yes, all as expected”). ROS owner/router loss while driving is prepared in ros_router_loss.sh (killed router: OwnerLost without lease stop; frozen router: lease stop, release and link-down), passing on loopback/CI. The board run passed both, and Todor confirmed all four wheels stopped and stayed still.

Physical evidence and deferrals

Task 5.2 disposition

On 2026-10-19 Todor instructed: “skip task 5.2 since we dont have good measurement tools”. Task 5.2 is closed with the completed evidence below retained and the remaining equipment-dependent checks skipped. Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband measurements and the coast/driven-neighbour check are deferred to a later change when suitable measurement tools are available. They have not passed physical validation; host pin-ordering and mapping tests remain software evidence only. No further board run is scheduled for task 5.2. This scope decision does not change the specified motor behavior. The task 5.3 review records acceptance within these limits.

Earlier product runs are development evidence: coordinator, validation and BLE reconnect. They used earlier firmware; they do not accept the current product. M4/M5 remain the comparison/rollback reference. Each physical motor run is announced separately and waits for Todor's go.

Laptop teleoperation verification

Physical acceptance — tasks 5.1/5.2

The separately authorized stand batch passed on the installed normal ROS firmware, without flashing. The actual terminal client performed five seconds idle, unarmed W, R at zero, six gentle directions with input-expiry pauses, forward/Space, unarmed W, explicit re-arm, fresh forward and Ctrl-D. Serial confirmed all six wheel patterns, zero at each pause, matching control acknowledgements and final STOP/release/Open. Capture stopped, previous Wi-Fi was restored and the internet route was unchanged. Todor confirmed: “Yes, all behaved as expected.” This includes all directions, every stop and still wheels through reset/startup and both unarmed checks.

This accepts the implemented application for supervised stand use. Malformed packets, refused/missing controls, lost links and scheduling failures remain covered by host tests; they were not injected into this physical batch. M6’s measurement deferrals remain unchanged; no electrical coast/STBY, current, temperature margin or loaded/floor result is claimed.

Shared codec container regression

The first #90 ROS CI run failed because the scenario compatibility import was mounted at /scenarios without the extracted apps/client package. The existing apps/simcar/scenarios/ros-capabilities.sh test reproduced IndexError: 3 locally before the fix. All three affected runners now mount scenarios and the shared codec in their repository layout inside the container. The same capabilities and reconnect test passes, as do ros_readonly.sh and default ros_stops.sh against loopback ROS simulators. The 31 client tests pass again. Firmware and UDP wire behavior are unchanged.

iPhone BLE web controller verification map

Scoped acceptance recorded 2026-10-21. H1–H5 pass on Linux under apps/iphone and in CI; phone/stand results are recorded below. Tasks retain the exact evidence and Todor's accepted limits. This supersedes the draft's pending-evidence summary; the original planned checks remain for traceability.

Recorded phone evidence

  • P1: Todor reported ten successful connect/zero-ARM/STOP cycles. A serial-captured five-cycle diagnosis measured ATT MTU 247 on iPhone 11 Pro/Bluefy. Earlier BLE drops were not reproduced.
  • P2: a reported 1,614-write (~80 s) run had max submission gap 158 ms and slowest write 17 ms. Todor closed P2 by decision; there is no serial-captured full workload, the earlier drops remain unexplained and the iOS connection interval is unmeasured. Closure is not a new reliability or timing measurement.
  • P3: touch, Home, lock, Bluetooth-off and reload checks reached zero/STOP or firmware link-loss stop; no background renewal or automatic reconnect was observed. VoiceOver was skipped.
  • P4: Todor confirmed all six directions and stops on the stand. STOP while holding was subsequently fixed on touch-down and rechecked with motor power off. Phone UI limits prevented Bluetooth-off during a held direction; no new physical stop-latency, electrical or floor qualification is claimed.

Linux host and browser evidence

ID Test boundary and completion evidence

Original planned Bluefy / normal product firmware checks

These are the original planned checks, not authorization to repeat them. Their completed results and accepted limits are recorded above and in tasks.md. Draft authoring itself performed no hardware work. Runs use normal default or ros firmware; never motor-bench or firmware changed merely to make Bluefy pass.

  • P1 — browser/claim/payload integration (I1/I2): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Record phone/iOS/Bluefy/web/firmware revisions, HTTPS origin, split with/without-response write APIs, explicit read promises/notifications, name-only picker and error behavior. Across 10 manual connections, verify validated setup and explicit ARM/STOP at zero with the expected fresh Status. The phone's 72-byte capability is user-confirmed; this checks our browser/firmware path. Record ATT MTU/capacity only if actually measured externally; unavailable MTU is not a browser failure or fabricated API result. Record claim timing and release observations separately.
  • P2 — full workload (I3/Q19): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Run 60 s at 20 Hz zero including Status polling and explicit ARM/STOP/re-arm at zero. Require no lease expiry, submission gap>=200 ms or one-second control/read timeout. Log pending-operation delays, promise durations, submission-gap distribution and read/control latency. Only actual instrumentation can establish connection interval; timer frequency/BlueZ cannot. Failing performance requires reviewed contract/approach changes before motor checks.
  • P3 — host lifecycle and usability (I1/I4): motor power disabled, separately authorized batch. Verify real pointer/hold/cancel/multi-touch, accessibility/text sizing, Bluefy browser controls, blur/page visibility, app switch/Home, lock/unlock, interruptions, Bluetooth off/on, permission changes, navigation, force termination/reload and unavailable peer. Record detected events, UI renewal expiry, last nonzero submission, cleanup attempts and device-reported state. P3 fails if an inactive host keeps renewing nonzero intent/streaming it; unsupported signals must not silently become a safety promise. Distinguish observed expiry/firmware fallback from runnable cleanup. Record non-inducible cases as unverified.
  • P4 — supervised wheel acceptance: only after P1–P3 and a separately announced batch with Todor's go, wheels off ground. Observe six directions briefly, release-to-zero, STOP during hold, new ARM/new press, lock/background and link loss. Record Todor's physical observations separately from browser/protocol/firmware logs. Confirm independent lease fallback; app deadlines are not physical stop bounds. No electrical/coast limits, floor speed accuracy, range or unattended-safety claim.

Record date, exact steps, hardware/browser/web/firmware identities, logs, observations and failures. Hardware policy and acceptance gates apply. Missing/failed evidence leaves its task unchecked; revised behavior returns to proposal review.

Next stand batch

Announced procedure (Todor subsequently gave “go”): rover on its stand, all wheels clear, motor bank awake and USB connected; use the same published 2b5104400362 build. No flash is needed. Capture serial output before enabling motor power. In Physical mode, capture neutral with Set neutral & ARM and use explicit START at neutral for each move.

  • Six single-axis moves: forward, backward, strafe left/right, rotate left/right.
  • Two blended moves: forward + left strafe; then forward + left strafe + left turn.
  • One forward move ending with STOP; verify a new ARM stays paused until START.
  • One forward move ending by switching to Buttons; verify disarm and stillness.

Each move lasts at most 2 s, with at least 3 s at zero between moves (at most 20 s of requested motion in total). For the first eight moves return to neutral, observe zero, then PAUSE. Use offsets up to 20° to check the displayed gentle caps of 0.1 m/s per translation axis and 0.3 rad/s rotation, subject to advertised limits. The final two moves exercise STOP and mode-change stopping while tilted. Finish with STOP/disconnect and motor power off. Any unexpected motion or failure to stop aborts the batch. Record serial commands separately from Todor's physical wheel confirmation; do not infer measured velocity or stopping time.

Stand result — partial

Todor reported “done. all moves performewd” for the authorized 2b5104400362 procedure. The capture and operator record show eight nonzero-command periods returning to zero, final STOP, release and Open at zero. No re-ARM or subsequent nonzero period appears; final STOP occurred after the last period had already reached zero. The final STOP/re-ARM and mode switch while moving were subsequently explicitly confirmed by Todor (“Also completed STOP/re-ARM and mode switching”). Record them as operator-confirmed functional behavior; the captured sequence does not independently show them, and the discrepancy remains unexplained. No Stream counters or raw twists were supplied; client caps and measured stopping are not inferred. Command periods include 5.281 s and 8.132 s, totaling 24.605 s, so the announced 2 s/20 s bounds are not recorded as passed. Capture is stopped; no firmware was flashed. Task 3.2 remains partial for client cap evidence; the final functional stop/re-ARM/ mode-switch checks are confirmed. No new drive is authorized.

Latest motor-power-off response: Todor reported the remaining phone procedure “completed” and that scrolling stops tilt control (record). Scroll-to-pause at zero with arm/neutral retained is intentional and covered by an existing browser regression. Todor clarified “Pauses; stays Armed and connected”, confirming that intended behavior on the phone. Requested cap values, Stream counters, versions, rotation message and permission-prompt outcome were not supplied. Tasks 3.1–3.3 remain open for their outstanding evidence; the scroll observation matches the control contract and requires no runtime fix.

Host evidence

apps/teleop/tests/test_ble.py uses a fake GATT peripheral and nonblocking input, plus actual CLI subprocesses with pseudo-terminals. No Bluetooth device is used.

The late-Echo test first failed (LinkError not raised) before the callback was changed to retain expired probes; the same command now passes. The full client suite also includes a test with three valid 110 ms GATT round trips that first failed as a scheduler stall; loop checks now run between operations. The suite also covers UDP protocol/runtime and the real product simulator. BLE tests run both without Bleak installed and with the project's Bleak 2.1.1 in nix-shell; optional BLE imports do not make UDP depend on Bleak.

Final host results: 59 client tests pass (29.236 s), including all 20 BLE tests; the same 20 BLE tests pass with Bleak 2.1.1 in Nix shell (9.581 s). Strict active/baseline specs and all six generated-reader checks pass.

Physical acceptance — passed 2026-10-22

Todor authorized the announced stand batch and confirmed “yes, all good” (evidence): ATT MTU 247, car AP off while connected and back on after release, no motion before R, all six directions followed by zero on expiry, Space/no-motion without R, a ~5 s laptop Bluetooth outage with no motion, one beep, Reconnected disarmed, discarded outage input and a fresh R/direction.

The first quit failed: cleanup reported STOP and disconnect unconfirmed (exit 1). A no-motion probe measured STOP write 75–124 ms, Status read 89–93 ms and BlueZ disconnect 2.1–2.6 s against 80/80/250 ms deadlines. The new latency test failed first; cleanup now shares one 500 ms budget and labels an unfinished disconnect requested (unconfirmed), which no longer fails the exit. The authorized quit re-run acknowledged STOP, exited 0 in 0.57 s, and serial showed release, link down and AP on ~2.3 s after STOP. Final host results: 60 client tests pass, including 21 BLE tests with Bleak 2.1.1.

Floor use, electrical/thermal measurements, physical stop timing and a bound on BLE recovery time (~13 s observed) remain outside scope.

openspec/changes/add-home-network-mode/proposal.md

Home network mode

Status: accepted for implementation on 2026-10-22 (Todor: “merge them and continue with next steps”, PR #107). No flash or motor run is authorized; each board step is announced separately.

Why

Rovi can only be driven from a device on its own access point (AP) or over BLE, so a ROS 2 controller must run on a laptop that has given up its normal Wi-Fi. Todor wants a controller running as a service on the home network to drive the car around the house and take part in the other ROS 2 activity there, while he can still take over by hand over BLE. This closes open question Q21 in PLAN.md.

What Changes

  • Home mode. At boot, if the firmware was built with home Wi-Fi settings, the car joins the home Wi-Fi as a station (DHCP) and connects to the configured ROS router. When both succeed it serves ROS 2 (and UDP) there (ADR-0011 auto-arm unchanged).
  • Fallback. If no settings were built in, the network is not seen in a ~1.5 s scan, or join + address + ROS router do not succeed within ~8 s, the car runs exactly today's AP behaviour. It stays there until reboot or a Home mode command. AP and station never run at the same time.
  • Mode command on every transport. A disarmed owner on BLE, UDP or ROS can choose Home or Car network; it takes effect when that ownership ends. So every mode is reachable from any one type of client, without reflashing or touching the car.
  • Network information on every transport. Mode, pending command, last fallback reason and the car's home IP, readable by owners and non-owners (BLE characteristic, UDP kind, ROS topic).
  • Takeover priority: BLE > UDP > ROS. UDP preempts a ROS owner in both modes; in home mode BLE (which keeps advertising) preempts UDP or ROS. Preemption stops the car and leaves the new owner disarmed. BREAKING for ADR-0004's first-claim rule.
  • Safe hand-back. When a manual takeover ends without a Home command (e.g. an accidental BLE drop), the next ROS owner must publish /rovi/arm true once before moving. With Home sent first, ROS takes over and auto-arms as today.
  • Protocol alignment. Every transport gets the same operations (todor, 2026-10-22):
    • BLE claims on its first Setpoint/Control write, not on connect, with up to two connections, so a BLE central can watch without claiming.
    • Capabilities, Status and network information are readable before claiming everywhere (UDP INFO, kind 11).
    • ROS gets an explicit release (/rovi/release) like UDP BYE and BLE disconnect.
    • A preempted owner receives a final Status (stopped, owner-lost) on its own transport.
    • One transport-independent scenario suite runs the shared rules over BLE, UDP and ROS in the simulator.
  • Router by name (Todor, 2026-10-28: “i want to resolve the router by name”). Accept IPv4 or a host name; resolve .local through mDNS and other names through DHCP DNS on every connection attempt, within the existing join budget. Literal endpoints remain supported.
  • Settings at build time. SSID, passphrase and the home ROS router endpoint are build variables, like today's ROVI_WIFI_PASSWORD, flashed over USB. Nothing about the home network is sent over the air.
  • Trust. Any device on the home network may control the car, with no new authentication (ADR-0008 station-mode exclusion superseded).
  • Observability. New log events report mode changes, mode commands and each join step with its duration.

Deferred: a shared Rust client crate for all clients (#108), the iPhone mode/network UI (#109). Out of scope: a ROS echo (router liveliness covers it), running AP and station together, UDP authentication, automatic router discovery via zenoh scouting, NTP/OTA, changing home settings without a reflash, automatic retry of home Wi-Fi from fallback, BLE preemption in fallback mode.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • network-mode: home/fallback selection, join budget, mode command and its errors on all transports, network information, hand-back latch, BLE availability in home mode, link loss, build-time settings and mode events.

Modified Capabilities

  • car-control-api: modified Single owner (BLE > UDP > ROS preemption), Explicit arming (hand-back latch), Capabilities and Status (readable before claiming), Echo is observational (BLE echo without claiming); added BLE claim on first command, Observation without ownership, ROS release and Takeover notice. Claim/reclaim windows, lease, stop rules and existing message encodings are unchanged.

Impact

  • Firmware: Wi-Fi station and DHCP (embassy-net dhcpv4), build variables ROVI_HOME_SSID, ROVI_HOME_PASSWORD, ROVI_HOME_ROUTER, a per-mode ROS router endpoint, one new GATT characteristic (Network), ROS topics /rovi/mode and /rovi/network. No new dependency or flash storage.
  • rovi-core: mode supervisor, arbiter preemption, hand-back latch, mode command and network-information codecs on all three transports, new log events; simulator and host tests.
  • Clients: laptop teleop gains --mode home|car and shows network information; the iPhone client keeps working unchanged (mode UI optional later).
  • Docs: new ADR superseding parts of ADR-0004 and ADR-0008; PLAN.md Q21 closed; glossary STA entry updated.
  • Acceptance needs board checks on a real home network, including BLE/Wi-Fi coexistence while ROS drives; each motor batch needs its own announced go.

openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/proposal.md

M6: low-level four-wheel API

Status: archived/synced 2026-10-20 after #87 merged in f5a2d8e; proposed 2026-10-10; laptop implementation scope accepted 2026-10-17 by Todor's merge of #48. Open items O1–O8 closed or deferred 2026-10-17. Scoped product acceptance is recorded on 2026-10-19 in the task 5.3 review, using Todor’s physical confirmations and explicit task 5.2 measurement deferrals. The product crates, sim car and firmware are implemented; laptop conformance and CI are tracked in tasks 1–3. Existing experiments remain the comparison/rollback reference; unverified physical limits below remain explicit. Terms are as defined in GLOSSARY.md.

Why

VISION layer 2 needs a product API that drives the car's four wheels independently, stays independent of transport and mecanum math, and fails safe. M8 (README) proved the transport and ownership model on the board. M4 added four physical motor outputs and verified stops, reversals and a thermal run; M5 demonstrated floor movement and recorded approximate motion references. This change turns that experimental behavior into a reusable product API, separating motor control from the device state machine. It reuses the working code and evidence rather than starting another firmware experiment.

What Changes

  • motor-control (new): the reusable layer that takes four wheel commands (FL, FR, RR, RL, normalised −1..1) and drives the motor drivers. It knows nothing of setpoints, kinematics or transports. It owns driver standby, the boot-safe state and the limits M4 measures.
  • car-control-api (new): the car's device control API, extracted from M8 with its explicit transport differences (including ROS auto-arm). This proposal corrects validation, ordering, fault recovery and status gaps described in the design; it does not claim behavior-identical extraction.
  • Firmware integration follows the accepted laptop implementation tasks; flashing and motor runs require separate authorization. BLE/UDP byte layouts and numeric codes stay as M8 defines them (README); this spec states behaviour, not wire formats.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • motor-control: independent wheel commands, driver standby, duty limits and fault handling.
  • car-control-api: setpoint processing, ownership, arming, lease, capabilities and status.

Modified Capabilities

None; this is the first product specification change.

Design decisions

  • The motor control boundary is normalised wheel commands, not SI wheel speeds. M5 confirmed no encoders; the current car uses open-loop duty control (Q11/O3, 2026-10-17). A normalised command survives both: 1.0 means the configured maximum, whether that is a duty or a wheel speed. The device layer still converts setpoints to SI wheel speeds first, as mecanum_drive_controller does (ADR-0006).
  • Controllers cannot send wheel commands directly. The device control API accepts setpoints only. Exposing four wheel velocities stays deferred, as ADR-0006 records; motor control is a firmware-internal boundary.
  • ROS 2 controllers read capabilities before claiming. A ROS 2 controller claims with its first setpoint, so it needs the limits before it claims. The car publishes /rovi/capabilities (std_msgs/String, key=value) without a claim. O9 selected the specified reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback: changes plus a 900 ms heartbeat; retained history was unavailable with the pinned publisher. Rejected: a custom message type (every controller must build a Rovi interface package) and ROS 2 parameters (they need services, which the car does not serve).
  • Safety is enforced twice. The device layer raises safety stops (ADR-0004); motor control independently holds standby until it is explicitly enabled and on any invalid wheel command.

Implementation boundaries, migration and the reviewed contract changes are in design.md. Existing ADRs remain authoritative; no new irreversible architectural decision is introduced.

Evidence and remaining decisions

Use M4 results, M5 results and the accepted motion references. Todor stopped the extended measurement sweep; no new motor tests are queued by this proposal. Approximate references are not guaranteed velocity tracking.

ID Status Answer
O1 Closed 2026-10-17 Duty limits stay configurable. The product profile caps drive duty at 70%, the envelope M4 verified on the bench (ten ±70% reversals, 5-minute thermal run, radio up). The experiment firmware's 100% is not a product value. Deferred, needs a current monitor (INA226) or an oscilloscope with a shunt: start and stall current. Needed only to raise the cap or to claim current protection; this change claims neither.
O2 Closed 2026-10-17 Measured geometry: radius 0.030 m, wheelbase 0.115 m, track 0.140 m, centre projection sum 0.1275 m. Open-loop with the accepted approximate motion references; no calibration sweep. The 40 rad/s normalization and 1/1/3 input limits stay in the profile, labelled experimental, not measured maxima. The references were recorded on the experiment's 40–100% mapping; under the 70% cap the same command gives less duty (vx 0.20: 45% instead of 50%). Maximum physical speeds are not claimed.
O3 Closed Open-loop duty control; no encoders, added sensing out of scope.
O4 Deferred, needs a logic analyzer or oscilloscope A numeric pin-level STBY disable bound. This change specifies and host-tests that a safety stop deasserts both STBY outputs in the control tick that processes it, before any further bridge update. M4 observed all four wheels stop on every trigger. No numeric bound is claimed.
O5 Closed 2026-10-17 Coast for an individual zero wheel (TB6612 IN1=IN2=low, PWM=high), standby for every safety stop. The experiment's all-low zero pins do not prove coast; task 2.1 corrects them test-first. Coast distance is not measured or claimed (tape and video, if a later requirement needs it).
O6 Closed Exact zero and magnitudes below 0.02 coast; other commands map linearly from 40% to the configured maximum. About 35% starting duty observed on the stand; no per-wheel threshold is claimed.
O7 Closed 2026-10-17 Direct reversals, no ramp, up to the 70% cap: M4's ten ±70% reversals caused no ESP32 reset or BLE loss. Raising the cap reopens O7 together with O1.
O8 Closed D1 A→FL, D1 B→RL, D2 A→FR, D2 B→RR; directions corrected at connectors, all software inversions false, reconfirmed after the motor rework. Each driver has its own STBY, both disabled on a safety stop.
O9 Closed 2026-10-17 The pinned ordinary publisher did not serve history to a late Jazzy transient-local subscriber (no sample within 3 s; its later live sample arrived). Selected the specified reliable/volatile/depth-1 fallback: every 900 ms (headroom under one second), on claim/release and reconnect. Late subscribers received in 0.413/0.551 s before/after router restart; probe and fallback evidence.

On 2026-10-19 Todor closed task 5.2 with the remaining equipment-dependent checks skipped because suitable measurement tools are unavailable. Coast/STBY pin levels, electrical duty/deadband measurements and the coast/driven-neighbour check remain physically unverified; they return in a later change with suitable tools. Completed board results are retained in the verification map; task 5.3 records acceptance within that scope. Specified motor behavior is unchanged.

No unresolved product decisions remain. Deferred items are outside this change: it does not claim measured current, a numeric disable bound, coast distance, maximum speeds or operation above 70%. Equipment-gated items return as a new change when the equipment is available. Retain the experiment firmware for comparison; product acceptance is a separate checklist.

First implementation scope

  • Reuse M8's core, motor mapping and tests in a shared Cargo workspace; isolate motor control from the arbiter and transports.
  • Add conformance tests for the specified deadband/duty rule, independent wheels, faults, standby and documented zero-output mode.
  • Keep BLE, UDP, optional ROS and the accepted ownership/arming policies. Apply the reviewed corrections and implement the agreed ROS capabilities and extended status topics.
  • No new encoder, camera, phone-app, station-mode or hardware-monitor work in this change.
  • Do not flash or start a motor test as part of extraction or host validation. Each board run is announced separately and waits for Todor's go.

Impact

  • Planning: openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-20-add-four-wheel-api/, following the product specification standard and ADR-0015.
  • Code: crates/rovi-core, crates/rovi-motor-control and crates/rovi-drive in the root workspace, with separate apps/simcar and firmware packages/lockfiles. The tasks and verification map record software checks, confirmed board results and explicit physical deferrals.
  • Evidence: host tests and the sim car are development evidence only (ADR-0002). The scoped acceptance review uses the product board runs linked in the verification map, preserving M4/M5 as references.

Review status

The 2026-10-17 review findings are addressed: ROS latch exceptions, complete motor fault/configuration recovery, clamped kinematics, shared Wi-Fi exclusion, explicit transport edge cases and ROS field/QoS contracts. The design and verification map accompany the requirements. Todor merged #48 on 2026-10-17, accepting the laptop implementation tasks (task 1.1). That does not establish product hardware acceptance or authorize a flash/motor run. The same day Todor agreed O1 and O2; O5 and O7 closed with them, and O4 and O1's current measurement are deferred as equipment-gated. O9 closed with the specified volatile fallback and recorded Jazzy evidence.

The 2026-10-19 final acceptance review completes task 5.3 for the recorded scope. It preserves the equipment-dependent checks Todor skipped as physically unverified; no new qualification claims or motor authorization follow from acceptance. The pinned CLI archived/synced this change on 2026-10-20 after the stack landed, creating the car control API and motor control baselines without changing requirement behavior. Measurements explicitly deferred at acceptance remain unverified.

Laptop UDP teleoperation

Status: implemented and accepted for supervised stand use on 2026-10-20. Why

The vision calls for teleoperation above the device API. M6 now provides that API, but the laptop tools are scenario/bench runners rather than an interactive product client.

What Changes

  • Add a Linux terminal client over the existing UDP protocol: explicit target, connect disarmed, explicit arm, six gentle directions, STOP and quit.
  • Bound each recognized motion key to a 250 ms input window; stream zeros when input expires, and clear motion on STOP, faults or communication failure. No automatic claim/re-arm after failure.
  • Reuse the tested TwistStamped, capability and Status codecs. Add deterministic policy tests, simulated UDP peers and product-simulator coverage before any separately authorized board test.
  • Preserve M6’s firmware, ownership, wire codes, lease and 70% product cap. No iPhone/BLE client, ROS controller, station mode, floor/autonomous behavior or new physical qualification claim in this change.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • laptop-teleoperation: interactive laptop input, client-side arming, bounded command streaming, status presentation and shutdown over the existing UDP API.

Modified Capabilities

None. The client consumes car-control-api; it does not alter that contract or motor-control.

Impact

  • Code: a small standard-library Python client under apps/teleop, a shared codec module, simulator tests and product usage instructions. No additional runtime dependency.
  • Existing Python wire-codec callers retain compatibility; Rust/firmware and experimental behavior remain unchanged.
  • Product implementation requires explicit proposal acceptance per SPECIFICATION. Each motor batch remains separately announced and authorized. M6’s measurement deferrals remain in effect.

Scope choice

Todor selected laptop UDP teleoperation on 2026-10-20. The proposed keys, gentle defaults and bounded-input policy define this reversible first client; Q9 and Q21 remain separate future work.

Implementation progress

The laptop client is implemented under apps/teleop, using shared apps/client payload codecs with the former import path preserved. Host protocol/policy, pseudo-terminal, fake-peer and product-simulator tests are linked in the verification map. CI includes the client suite. The separate stand batch passed on 2026-10-20 with Todor’s explicit wheel observations (evidence). The application is accepted for this supervised stand scope; no new measurement, firmware change, flash or loaded/floor result is claimed.

iPhone BLE web controller proposal

Why

Rovi's vision includes an iPhone controller, but the accepted product has only laptop clients. Todor has Linux, no Mac or Apple Developer Program membership, and prefers no subscription. A browser controller can use the existing BLE API without building or signing a new iOS app; see roadmap Q9/Q18/Q19.

What Changes

  • Target an HTTPS web controller opened in the free Bluefy iPhone browser, selected by Todor in this conversation. Standard Safari is not a supported BLE host. Develop and test the web code from Linux; no Xcode, native scaffold or signing workflow.
  • Use browser-mediated explicit device selection/connect, visible capabilities and last-reported Status. Connect disarmed; require fresh zero then explicit ARM before six gentle press-and-hold directions become usable.
  • Buttons are the selected first input method. Keep input interpretation separate from the bounded motion/session policy so a later accelerometer/tilt input can use the same limits, ARM, STOP and expiry rules. Sensor control, sensor permissions and calibration are deferred, not implemented in v1.
  • Bound hold age, stream stalls and cleanup. Page/host interruption or link failure clears motion; no automatic reconnect, re-arm or motion replay. Validate Bluefy's lifecycle behavior on the actual phone before accepting control.
  • Todor confirms the phone can send the 72-byte payload. Retain runtime failure handling and separate browser/firmware integration evidence from that user-reported phone capability; no new MTU measurement is claimed. Streaming-rate Q19 remains open.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

  • iphone-ble-teleoperation: iPhone browser discovery/selection, ownership, explicit arming, touch control, interruption handling and honest feedback through the existing BLE interface.

Modified Capabilities

None. Car control API, motor control and laptop teleoperation retain their accepted contracts.

Impact

Future implementation would be static HTML/CSS/JavaScript under apps/iphone/, using Web Bluetooth in Bluefy with no third-party runtime scripts or command server. Propose repository GitHub Pages hosting; verify the final origin/HTTPS during delivery. Existing normal product firmware (default or ros, never motor-bench), GATT UUIDs and codecs remain unchanged. BLE connection itself claims ownership and switches off the car AP; a picker alone does not claim. Missing advertisements do not prove another owner exists.

Specification PR #95 contains planning Markdown only; the button controller lands in a stacked implementation PR under apps/iphone/. Neither publishes hosting, runs device/network tests or changes firmware. Native iOS build/signing, Wi-Fi diagnostics, station mode, BLE credential provisioning (Q21), compact setpoints, pairing/authentication changes, background driving, mixed-axis controls and sensor driving are outside v1.

Proposal acceptance

Accepted for button-based implementation (2026-10-20). In this conversation Todor answered the explicit proposal question with: “Accept proposal and implement buttons”. This accepts the revised Bluefy requirements in PR #95 at b80e673a085d84c6d6dcd87c031194b5e7912bf4, with accelerometer control deferred. Task 1.1 records that evidence. Product/phone/wheel acceptance remains pending; no deployment or physical test is claimed or authorized by this record. Parent retains merge coordination. Implementation proceeds on the stacked feat/iphone-ble-web branch.

Review the design/OPEN questions, requirements, tasks and verification map. Implementation progress and evidence are tracked there; physical acceptance remains pending.

iPhone physical control

Why

Todor wants the existing iPhone client to offer button and three-axis physical control. The isolated phone test confirms sensor access and the intended local interaction; it does not establish sensor-plus-BLE or motor acceptance.

What Changes

  • Add a Buttons / Physical selector, defaulting to Buttons without persistence.
  • In Physical mode, explicitly enable orientation sensors, then capture neutral and ARM in one tap while disarmed, followed by an explicit START at neutral. Combine forward/back tilt, strafe tilt and heading offset into gentle vx/vy/wz. Holding a twist sustains rotation.
  • Block motion on unavailable input; sensor/posture loss while driving ends the session. Paused sensor gaps or reading posture retain neutral and arm at zero. Preserve STOP, stream, cleanup and lifecycle recovery. Keep safety status and STOP visible while scrolling.
  • Keep the isolated diagnostic available and separate phone/radio/motor evidence.

Capabilities

New Capabilities

None.

Modified Capabilities

  • iphone-ble-teleoperation: selectable button/physical input, calibration, bounded blended velocities, independent sample/foreground expiry and mode switching.

Impact

apps/iphone/ input, session and UI code, tests, static build and documentation. No new dependency, wire format, firmware or native app. Physical mode is supported initially for portrait, screen-up use near the phone posture tested by Todor.

Proposal acceptance

Todor explicitly requested the same-client mode switch and all three mappings, then chose angle-from-neutral rotation on 2026-10-21. After the sensor-only run, he confirmed the three previews, held twist and neutral/release behavior, with expiry only during deliberate interruptions. This authorizes the selected host implementation. Phone evidence records the partial export, 13.1 s quiet sample and timing limits. Motor tests still require a separately announced batch and fresh go; acceptance/archive are not implied by this implementation authorization.

The first motor-power-off integrated test passed directions, neutral/release, STOP and switching. Todor then reported unwanted disarming during scrolling, hidden status and the unnecessary separate calibration tap. This authorizes the one-tap neutral/ARM and released-pad UX correction. Todor subsequently confirmed the announced corrected phone retest on build 780f65eff594 works with motor power off. He subsequently confirmed a 60 s neutral hold at requested zero on iPhone 11: 1,366 writes, max gap 180 ms, slowest write 19 ms. The original Bluefy trigger remains unclassified; remaining phone interruption/recovery and motor-on acceptance remain open.

Todor then reported posture-triggered disarming and difficulty keeping the drive pad pressed while moving the phone, explicitly requesting a different interface. Replace only Physical mode's held pad with tap START/PAUSE, a neutral prerequisite for START and a separate frame-renewal deadline. Buttons retain press-and-hold. Keep the existing posture limits and identify the exact failing angle in messages; the reported rotation/drop-of-touch cause is not yet established. This UI change requires another motor-power-off retest; earlier held-pad results remain historical.

Todor additionally requested a production-quality iPhone controller UI for both modes using design skills. This authorizes a compact responsive redesign, native segmented mode selection, clear state/feedback, a persistent action/STOP dock, collapsible diagnostics and sensor setup on explicit Physical selection. Preserve control safety and existing hosting; validate new usability on phone before acceptance.

Product acceptance — 2026-10-22

After accepting the redesigned UI and confirming phone/stand behavior, Todor explicitly selected “Accept tested scope; defer remaining checks”. Physical mode is accepted for supervised use on the reported iPhone setup, calibrated in the tested portrait/screen-up posture. The acceptance review records completed functional checks and deferred phone cap/Stream numbers, native rotation/permission outcomes and phone-only fault injection. Historical timing, capture discrepancies, duration overruns and unmeasured stopping remain explicit; this does not claim wider device, floor-use or measured stopping qualification.
